td.tagline: Comfortable banking with flexible mortgage solutions.
td.seoDescription: Compare TD mortgage rates today: fixed, variable, and special offers from our latest scrape, including how TD bank refinance rates differ from a straight renewal. The table is the rate source — confirm the contract with TD.
td.heroIntro: Compare current TD mortgage rates in Canada. Live fixed, variable, and special offers are in the table on this page.
td.overview:
TD Bank (Toronto-Dominion) is one of Canada's Big Five banks and a full-service mortgage lender with a large branch and digital network. Most shoppers meet TD as a direct lender: you apply with a mortgage specialist, online, or through an existing TD relationship rather than treating it as a broker-only monoline. The product set covers closed fixed and variable mortgages, refinances, and the TD Home Equity FlexLine, which pairs a traditional mortgage portion with a revolving home-equity line of credit.

TD is often chosen for convenience and prepayment flexibility (commonly cited as increasing payments by up to 100% and making annual lump-sum prepayments up to 15% of the original principal—confirm the current product sheet). It is less often the cheapest 5-year rate on a blind comparison against monolines. Use the live table on this page as the rate source; do not treat marketing copy as a quote. Then check GDS and TDS with the stress test calculator before you rely on a pre-approval.

td.whoItsFor:
TD mortgages tend to fit borrowers who already bank at TD, want in-person specialists, or need a bundled setup (chequing, credit cards, and a mortgage in one institution). The FlexLine is aimed at homeowners who want to keep unused equity available without a separate refinance every time they need funds.

TD is a weaker fit if your only goal is the lowest advertised 5-year rate and you are happy using a broker and a monoline. Big-bank credit, income, and property rules still apply, including the federal qualifying-rate test on new purchases and refinances. Estimate payment room with the mortgage affordability calculator using a TD rate from the table above, then check GDS/TDS with the stress test calculator. Newcomers with limited Canadian credit should ask specifically about TD's newcomer documentation—not assume every branch will structure the same deal.

products.title: Closed fixed-rate mortgages
products.description: Payment stays the same for the term (commonly 1–5 years, sometimes longer). Useful if you want a known payment and are comparing the 5-year fixed market. IRD or three-month interest penalties can apply if you break early.

products.title: Closed variable-rate mortgages
products.description: Rate moves with TD's prime. Your payment or the split between principal and interest will change with prime, depending on product. Still qualified at the stress-test rate, not at prime minus a discount.

products.title: TD Home Equity FlexLine
products.description: A readvanceable-style product: a mortgage segment plus a HELOC segment, typically capped by combined loan-to-value rules (often discussed as up to 80% combined, with the revolving portion limited further). Confirm current LTV caps with TD; they are policy, not a promise on this page.

products.title: Refinance and switch
products.description: TD can refinance an existing mortgage or receive a switch. A refinance, or a switch that adds funds or extends the amortization, is stress-tested. An uninsured straight switch at renewal, with the same amount and amortization, is not subject to OSFI’s prescribed stress test (November 21, 2024). Run the refinance calculator before you pay a penalty to move.

td.howRatesCompare:
TD's posted rates are not the rates most qualified borrowers pay. Special or discounted offers are what belong in a comparison. The cards and matrix at the top of this page are pulled from our rate feed—use those figures, not a round number from an old article.

On a vanilla 5-year closed mortgage, TD often sits with other large banks: convenient, relationship-priced, and frequently a bit higher than aggressive monolines. That gap can shrink if you have a strong TD relationship, a high-ratio insured deal, or a FlexLine structure the bank wants to book. Always compare the same term, insured vs uninsured, and the same prepayment rules. Start with 5-year fixed and variable hubs, then check digital channels such as Wealthsimple mortgage rates before you assume a bank special is the market low.
shoppingTips: Ask for the discounted rate in writing (term, insured vs uninsured, and whether cash-back is attached). Posted rate is a starting point, not the deal.
If you hold other TD products, ask whether relationship pricing applies—and what happens to the rate if you later move your chequing account.
Map FlexLine fees, HELOC prime spread, and the split between the term mortgage and the line of credit before you choose it over a simple closed mortgage.

At renewal, get TD's offer first, then compare it to the live table on our homepage. Staying skips a new stress test. An uninsured straight switch to another federally regulated lender does too, since OSFI's November 21, 2024 change, if the amount and amortization do not increase. A refinance or added funds still triggers it.
Confirm current prepayment privileges on the exact product (the widely cited 15% lump sum and 100% payment increase are not universal across every TD mortgage vintage).
Run GDS/TDS yourself with the affordability calculator and stress test calculator using TD's offered contract rate, then compare the actual payment with the mortgage payment calculator.

faqs.question: Does TD usually have the lowest mortgage rate in Canada?
faqs.answer: Often no. TD is a full-service bank. On a plain 5-year closed mortgage, monoline lenders and some credit unions frequently advertise lower contract rates. TD can still win on convenience, FlexLine structure, or a relationship discount. Compare the live TD rates on this page with the 5-year fixed and variable hubs rather than assuming a bank rate is the market low.

faqs.question: What is the TD Home Equity FlexLine?
faqs.answer: It combines a traditional mortgage portion with a revolving home equity line of credit. You pay down the mortgage segment and, subject to the product rules, can re-borrow available credit without a brand-new application each time. Combined loan-to-value limits apply. It is more flexible than a simple closed mortgage and more complex to compare on rate alone.

faqs.question: Can I get a TD mortgage through a mortgage broker?
faqs.answer: TD is primarily a direct-to-consumer bank. Many brokers cannot book TD the way they book monolines. If you want TD specifically, plan to talk to a TD mortgage specialist or apply through TD's own channels, then still compare the offer against brokered lenders.

faqs.question: What prepayment privileges does TD advertise?
faqs.answer: TD commonly describes the ability to increase regular payments by up to 100% and to make lump-sum prepayments of up to 15% of the original principal each year, without a penalty. Privileges are product-specific and can differ on older books, cash-back mortgages, or promotions. Read the commitment letter.

faqs.question: Does TD offer mortgages for newcomers to Canada?
faqs.answer: TD has newcomer-focused mortgage programs that can use alternative documentation when Canadian credit history is thin. Eligibility, down-payment, and income rules are set by TD and by default insurers on high-ratio deals. Bring immigration status, foreign credit, and down-payment source documents to a specialist rather than relying on a website summary.

faqs.question: Should I renew with TD or switch lenders?
faqs.answer: Renewing with TD usually avoids a new stress test. Since November 21, 2024, OSFI also does not require the stress test on an uninsured straight switch to another federally regulated lender at renewal when the loan amount and remaining amortization do not increase. Insured straight switches were already exempt. A refinance or added funds still triggers the test. If another lender's rate is meaningfully lower after penalties and fees, a straight switch can pay even when you would not pass the stress test on a larger loan.

faqs.question: What are TD bank refinance rates?
faqs.answer: TD bank refinance rates are the discounted fixed and variable specials in the table at the top of this page, not TD's posted rate. A refinance, or a switch that adds funds or extends the amortization, is qualified at the federal stress-test rate: the greater of the contract rate plus 2 percentage points or the 5.25 floor. An uninsured straight switch into TD at renewal, with the same amount and amortization, is not — OSFI stopped requiring that prescribed rate on November 21, 2024. Insured straight switches were already exempt. Renewing an existing TD mortgage with TD usually does not require a new stress test. Compare the live rows with the TD vs RBC page before you pay a penalty to move, and estimate the break cost with the penalty and refinance calculators.

faqs.question: Where can I check TD mortgage affordability?
faqs.answer: The GDS, TDS, and qualifying-rate rules are the same whether you use TD's tools or ours. Take a contract rate from the table on this page, then use the affordability calculator and the stress test calculator. Those tools sit with the other calculators; they are not the rate.

extraSections.heading: TD bank refinance rates
extraSections.html:
TD bank refinance rates are the fixed and variable specials in the table at the top of this page. Do not use TD's posted rate, and do not look for a refinance percentage written into this paragraph — if it is not in the scrape, we do not have it.

A refinance with TD pays out your current mortgage and starts a new one. If you are leaving another lender early, or breaking a TD term early, a penalty may apply. A refinance, or a switch that adds funds or extends the amortization, is qualified at the federal stress-test rate: the greater of the contract rate plus 2 percentage points or the 5.25 floor. An uninsured straight switch into TD at renewal, with the same amount and the remaining amortization not extended, is not: OSFI stopped requiring that prescribed rate on November 21, 2024. Insured straight switches were already exempt. Renewing an existing TD mortgage and staying at TD also skips a new stress test.

Put the live TD row next to TD vs RBC and the 5-year fixed hub before you pay a penalty. Estimate the break cost with the penalty calculator and whether the new payment wins with the refinance calculator.

scotiabank.name: Scotiabank
scotiabank.tagline: A Big Six bank whose STEP plan keeps equity available as the mortgage shrinks.
scotiabank.seoDescription: Scotiabank mortgage rates, the Scotia Total Equity Plan, and how a STEP collateral charge differs from a conventional Scotia Mortgage Corporation charge. The table is the live scrape.
scotiabank.heroIntro: Scotiabank is The Bank of Nova Scotia. The rate block above is our scrape. The product that actually changes the contract is usually the Scotia Total Equity Plan, not the headline fixed rate.
scotiabank.overview:
Scotiabank is one of Canada's Big Six banks. You book a retail mortgage with the bank itself: a branch advisor, a mobile advisor, or Scotiabank's own application. Do not assume an independent broker can place a Scotia file the way they place a monoline. Ask before you wait on that channel.

The product that separates Scotia from a plain closed loan is the Scotia Total Equity Plan (STEP). STEP is one borrowing plan secured by the house. Inside it you can hold mortgage components and a ScotiaLine personal line of credit. As principal comes off a mortgage component, room can open on the line, so cash you prepay is not automatically trapped in the walls. Scotia's own description says you can point prepayment privileges at the component you want to shrink. Go past the annual limit and the ordinary prepayment charge still applies.

Security is the part borrowers skip. Scotiabank registers either a collateral charge in favour of The Bank of Nova Scotia or a conventional charge in favour of Scotia Mortgage Corporation, a wholly owned subsidiary. A conventional charge puts the amount, term, and rate on title and secures only that mortgage. A collateral charge usually leaves those details in a separate credit agreement, can be registered for more than you borrow today, and may secure other Scotia debt. Scotia's charge comparison says that if you already have STEP and you want a second charge from someone else, the bank will ask you to close the STEP. In Quebec, borrowing more later can still mean a refinance or a new registration even when the collateral charge was registered high. A discharge of a collateral charge waits until every loan it secures is repaid, not merely the mortgage piece.

Prepayment room is not one number for every Scotia mortgage. The bank's mortgage disclosure describes annual lump-sum room and payment-increase room of 10 percent, 15 percent, or 20 percent of the original principal, depending on the solution you were sold, plus a Match-a-Payment option that can double a scheduled payment. Unused room does not roll into the next year. A closed fixed break is the greater of three months' interest and an interest-rate differential. A variable payout is typically three months' interest, and the same disclosure says you may be able to lock a variable into a longer fixed term without that charge. On a term longer than five years, once you pass the fifth anniversary the charge is capped at three months' interest. Some Scotia standard terms measure the differential using a current rate minus the discount you were given, which is the pattern that inflates a break fee. Run Scotia's own prepayment calculator, then read the information box on the commitment. The method on that box wins.

scotiabank.whoItsFor:
STEP fits a household that will actually redraw equity: renovations, a tax bill, a short gap between a sale and a purchase. The branch relationship matters if you want one institution to hold chequing, the mortgage, and the line. A conventional Scotia Mortgage Corporation charge is the cleaner file if you expect to move the loan at maturity and you do not want a global charge sitting on title.

Look elsewhere if the only goal is the cheapest five-year special from a broker, or if you may need a second mortgage from another lender while Scotia still holds STEP. Tangerine is a separate bank that Scotiabank owns. A Tangerine mortgage is not a STEP component and does not inherit this charge language. New purchases and refinances at a federally regulated bank still face the qualifying-rate rules described in the stress-test guide.

products.title: Closed fixed mortgage
products.description: Payment and rate stay put for the term you pick. Breaking it costs the greater of three months' interest and an interest-rate differential. Ask whether your solution's privilege band is 10, 15, or 20 percent before you compare it with a monoline's 15 or 20 percent.

products.title: Closed variable mortgage
products.description: The rate follows Scotiabank prime. A full payout is typically three months' interest. Scotia's disclosure says a lock-in to a longer fixed term can be available without a prepayment charge. Confirm that on the variable you are offered, not on a brochure.

products.title: Scotia Total Equity Plan
products.description: One plan, several credit pieces, secured by the home. The line can refill as you pay a mortgage component down. The registered collateral amount, the global limit, and whether other Scotia debts are caught by the same charge are in the STEP documents, not in this paragraph.

products.title: Open term
products.description: Scotia's disclosure describes an open mortgage you can pay out with an administration fee in the first year (the document states $200) and without a prepayment charge after that. The rate is usually worse than a closed term. Use it when you know the loan will die inside a year.

scotiabank.howRatesCompare:
Our Scotiabank scrape is often a short list. If the block above shows a single five-year fixed marked uninsured, that is the cell we captured, not the full menu a Home Financing Advisor can price. An empty variable or insured slot means the feed did not include it.

Scotia, like the other large banks, publishes posted rates and then discounts. Compare a written special, same term and same insured or uninsured label, with the five-year fixed hub and with a brokered monoline. A tenth of a point is the wrong thing to win if the charge is collateral and you might sell in year three. Read posted versus discounted rates before you treat the posted card as the offer.
shoppingTips: Ask, in writing, whether this file will be a STEP collateral charge or a Scotia Mortgage Corporation conventional charge, and what amount will be registered.
Get the privilege band (10, 15, or 20 percent) and whether Match-a-Payment is on this solution. Do not borrow the number from a friend's Scotia mortgage.
If a second mortgage or a private second is even a possibility, do not register STEP and hope the other lender can slot in behind it.
Price the break with Scotia's prepayment calculator, then ask whether the differential uses your discount. The penalty guide shows why that choice moves the fee by thousands.
At maturity, a straight renewal stays at Scotia. Moving a collateral charge to another lender usually means a lawyer, not a simple assignment. The switch guide is the checklist.

extraSections.heading: What the STEP charge does to a later move
extraSections.html:
A conventional charge can often be assigned to the next lender when you switch at maturity, which is why monolines like a standard charge. STEP's collateral charge is registered to the bank, often above the amount you owe, and Scotia has said it will ask you to close STEP before someone else registers a second charge. That is a feature when you want to re-borrow from Scotia without a new registration (Quebec excepted, where a new registration can still be required). It is a cost when you want to leave. Legal fees to discharge and re-register land on you unless the new lender agrees to pay them.

None of that shows up in the rate cell. If you are choosing between a Scotia special and a lower monoline rate, write down three numbers: the contract rate, the registered charge type, and whether you expect to sell or refinance before maturity. Then read banks, monolines, and credit unions.

faqs.question: Is a Scotiabank mortgage a STEP mortgage?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. STEP is the readvanceable plan that can hold a mortgage and a line of credit together. Scotiabank also registers ordinary conventional mortgages in the name of Scotia Mortgage Corporation. Ask which one is on the commitment. The rate table on this page does not tell you.

faqs.question: Can I put a second mortgage behind a STEP?
faqs.answer: Scotiabank's charge comparison says that if you have STEP and you want to register a second charge, the bank will request that you close the STEP. A collateral charge can also secure other Scotia debt, and a discharge waits until those debts are gone too. Plan the exit before you register the plan.

faqs.question: How much can I prepay on a Scotiabank mortgage without a charge?
faqs.answer: It depends on the solution. Scotia's disclosure describes annual lump-sum and payment-increase privileges of 10, 15, or 20 percent of the original principal, and a Match-a-Payment feature that can double a payment. The band is in your agreement. Unused room does not carry forward.

faqs.question: How does Scotiabank calculate a fixed-mortgage penalty?
faqs.answer: On a closed fixed term the charge is the greater of three months' interest and an interest-rate differential. Some Scotia terms build that differential from a current rate minus the discount you received, which is harsher than comparing your contract rate with today's contract rate. After five years of a longer term, the charge is capped at three months' interest. Use Scotia's calculator for an estimate and the commitment for the formula.

faqs.question: Do I get a Scotiabank mortgage through a broker?
faqs.answer: Retail Scotia mortgages are arranged with Scotiabank. Many brokers cannot submit them. If a broker says they can, ask which legal entity will be on title and whether the product is STEP. Otherwise apply with the bank and still compare the written special with the live rows on this page.

faqs.question: Why is the Scotiabank table on this page so short?
faqs.answer: We publish what the scrape returns. Scotiabank's public rate card is often just a posted or special fixed term, while variable, insured, and STEP pricing is quoted on a file. A blank cell is a missing scrape, not a statement that the product does not exist.

nationalbank.name: National Bank of Canada
nationalbank.tagline: Montreal-based Big Six bank with an All-in-One that splits a loan from a line of credit.
nationalbank.seoDescription: National Bank mortgage rates and the All-in-One: line-only, loan-plus-line, or a straight mortgage. See the 10 percent prepayment and the fixed-rate penalty that adds a capped interest month to the differential.
nationalbank.heroIntro: National Bank of Canada is a Big Six bank run from Montreal. The rows above are the uninsured terms in our latest scrape. The All-in-One is a different contract from that rate card.
nationalbank.overview:
National Bank of Canada is a Schedule I bank and one of the Big Six. Its retail network is thickest in Quebec, with branches and advisors in other provinces as well. You apply with the bank. A broker might still shop you against National Bank, but the mortgage is the bank's product, underwritten to the bank's policy, not a monoline the broker can freely reprice.

The home-equity product is the All-in-One, and National Bank publishes it as three different shapes, not one slogan. A line of credit on its own is aimed at borrowers who can leave more than 35 percent of the property value unfinanced, because the revolving portion is described as financing up to 65 percent of value. A made-to-measure version pairs a term loan with a line: the line still caps around 65 percent of value, and with more than 20 percent down the loan piece covers what the line does not. A straight mortgage loan is the ordinary amortizing contract, available with a smaller down payment, and repaid principal does not come back as credit. The product page lists a fee of $7 per month per account on the line versions. Confirm that fee on the current page before you treat a slightly lower rate as cheaper than a bank with no monthly account charge.

When a term loan is integrated into the All-in-One, principal you pay on that loan can become available credit on the line, generally within a day or two of a lump-sum prepayment and on a similar lag for a regular payment drawn from another institution. The line itself has no prepayment charge. Only interest is mandatory on the revolving portion. The term-loan portion still has a payment schedule and a penalty if you break it.

On an ordinary closed mortgage, National Bank's prepayment guide allows up to 10 percent of the original principal each calendar year, in one or several payments, with no fee. You can also add as much as one full regular payment on a payment date. Neither privilege carries forward, and the 10 percent privilege does not cover a full payout. Increasing payment frequency to weekly or biweekly accelerated is the third lever, and the bank notes that a second request to change frequency can attract a fee. A fixed-rate break is the higher of three months' interest, or one month of interest capped at $500 plus the interest differential. A variable-rate break is three months' interest. That "one month, maximum $500, plus the differential" structure is not how most of the other big banks write the clause. Read it before you rank National Bank on rate alone.

nationalbank.whoItsFor:
National Bank suits borrowers who live where the bank actually has advisors, especially in Quebec, and who want either a plain mortgage or a deliberate split between a term loan and a revolving line. The made-to-measure All-in-One is for someone who wants part of the debt on a fixed schedule and part of it redrawable, and who will notice a monthly account fee.

It is a weak fit if you need the line but you are putting less than 20 percent down, because that version of the All-in-One is described for buyers above that equity line. It is also a weak fit if you are rate-shopping a high-ratio insured five-year and the bank's public card, which on this site is an uninsured list, is not the product you will sign. Insured qualification still follows the insurer. Walk through the stress-test guide with the contract rate you were actually offered.

products.title: All-in-One, line only
products.description: Revolving credit up to 65 percent of value, for borrowers who can support a down payment above 35 percent. You set the payment above the interest. Repaid principal comes back as available credit. No prepayment charge on the line. The product page shows a monthly account fee.

products.title: All-in-One, loan plus line
products.description: More than 20 percent down. The line covers up to 65 percent of value and the term loan covers the rest. You can put the loan portion on a fixed rate, a variable rate, or a mix. Principal paid on the loan can replenish the line. The loan portion keeps its own prepayment rules.

products.title: Term mortgage
products.description: A closed loan with a set payment. Repaid principal does not become a line of credit unless you later refinance. Annual room is 10 percent of the original principal, plus up to one extra regular payment. Fixed and variable can be combined on the loan.

products.title: Ways to move the loan when you sell
products.description: National Bank's prepayment guide describes a buyer referral, a double mortgage when the new loan is at least twice the old balance, and a rollover that moves balance, rate, and remaining term onto a new National Bank mortgage. Each one has conditions, applies to new mortgage financing, and the guide says All-in-One and personal credit are excluded. Ask if the option is still open. The guide says these can change.

nationalbank.howRatesCompare:
The National Bank cells on this page are uninsured terms from the scrape, typically a shorter fixed, a five-year fixed, and a five-year variable when those rows are published. There is no insured column in that feed. Do not invent one by copying another bank's high-ratio special.

Stack the same term and the same uninsured label against the five-year fixed and variable hubs, and against Desjardins if the property is in Quebec. National Bank's own site still shows a posted shelf that can sit above the special a branch will write. The gap between those two numbers is the subject of the posted-versus-discounted guide. A lower special that uses the bank's fixed-penalty formula can still lose to a slightly higher rate whose break fee is three months' interest only.
shoppingTips: Name the All-in-One version before you talk rate. Line-only, loan-plus-line, and a straight mortgage are different equity tests.
Ask for the $7 account fee in the same quote as the rate. A monthly fee on a line changes the cost of a small balance.
On a fixed term, ask the advisor to show both pieces of the penalty: three months' interest, and one month of interest capped at $500 plus the differential. Keep the higher one.
If you might sell mid-term, ask whether buyer referral, double mortgage, or rollover would apply to your file, and get the exclusion for All-in-One in writing if that is what you hold.
Quebec files use a notary and an immovable hypothec. Budget that in the closing-cost calculator with the right province. It is not an Ontario lawyer bill.

extraSections.heading: The fixed penalty is the reason to read the clause
extraSections.html:
Most big-bank fixed mortgages charge the greater of three months' interest and an interest-rate differential, full stop. National Bank's repayment page writes the fixed charge as the higher of three months' interest, or one month of interest to a maximum of $500 plus the interest differential. The cap is on that one month, not on the differential. When rates have fallen, the differential is still the large number. When rates have not fallen, the three-month figure may win, and the extra month never comes into play. Either way, do not compare National Bank with a monoline using the contract rate alone.

The penalty guide and the penalty calculator show the arithmetic. They will not reproduce National Bank's exact comparison rate. For a payout figure, use the bank.

faqs.question: What is the National Bank All-in-One?
faqs.answer: It is a home-equity plan with three published shapes: a line of credit alone (up to 65 percent of value, aimed at buyers with more than 35 percent equity), a term loan plus a line (more than 20 percent down, line still capped near 65 percent), or a straight mortgage. The line has no prepayment charge. A term-loan portion does. The product page lists a $7 monthly fee per line account.

faqs.question: Does paying the mortgage give me the money back?
faqs.answer: On a straight mortgage, no. You would refinance to pull cash out. On an integrated All-in-One loan, National Bank says principal you repay can become available on the line, often within 24 to 48 hours for a lump sum. The line portion is revolving from the start.

faqs.question: How large is the penalty-free prepayment?
faqs.answer: Up to 10 percent of the original principal each calendar year, plus as much as one extra regular payment on a payment date. Unused room expires. A full payout, a refinance, an early renegotiation, or a transfer to another institution can still trigger a charge.

faqs.question: Is National Bank only a Quebec lender?
faqs.answer: No. It is a national Schedule I bank. The branch network and the everyday mortgage conversation are deepest in Quebec. If you are buying in another province, confirm the bank will take the property and that you can reach an advisor, then compare the offer with lenders that are built for that market.

faqs.question: Can I avoid the penalty if I sell?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. The prepayment guide describes a buyer referral, a double-mortgage rebate when the new National Bank loan is large enough, and a rollover onto a new purchase. Conditions apply, the guide says the options can change, and it excludes All-in-One and other non-mortgage credit. Ask before you waive a condition on the sale.

nesto.heroIntro: nesto shows its rates in public and arranges the mortgage online. The four cells above, when the scrape has them, are the only nesto numbers on this page.
nesto.overview:
nesto is a Canadian mortgage company with its head office in Montreal. It is not a Big Six bank and it is not a credit union. Its own FAQ calls it a digital mortgage lending platform that screens the market for a rate and then has the file handled inside nesto. Its licence page tells a more precise story. nesto Inc. holds mortgage brokerage and, in several provinces, administrator registrations. Nova Scotia's row lists brokerage, lender, and administrator. Ontario is brokerage number 13044 and administrator number 13503. The footer also names British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island, and the three territories. The Quebec line on that table is marked not applicable under the Act respecting the distribution of financial products and services. If your property is in Quebec, ask nesto which legal entity would fund or arrange the loan rather than assuming the brokerage row covers it.

That split matters. When nesto funds and services the mortgage, nesto is the lender. When another lender's product fits, nesto is the broker. The commitment names the lender. Our rate table cannot. nesto also owns CMLS, acquired on 20 June 2024, and CMLS still originates under its own name through brokers. A nesto application is not automatically a CMLS mortgage. Read the CMLS page if a broker is placing the file there.

The sales model is the other half of the pitch. nesto says its mortgage experts are salaried, not paid a commission on the product you pick. A quarterly bonus can exist, and nesto says that bonus is not tied to the solution or the rate the client chooses. The "Low Mortgage Rate Guarantee" on the homepage is nesto's phrase for showing the lowest applicable rate at the start, without a negotiation. It is not the "beat a competitor or pay a flat cash amount" promise some brokerages publish. Treat it as a description of how they open the file. The rate you sign is still the one on the commitment, for the term and the insured or uninsured label you qualified for.

Two features show up on nesto's own FAQ as standing offers rather than as a one-week banner: a rate hold of up to 150 days on most mortgage solutions, and a 1 percent cash-back option on its mortgage solutions. Holds and cash-back have conditions, and both can be revised. Ask which of your terms are eligible, whether cash-back changes the contract rate, and whether the hold includes a float-down if market rates fall. The homepage also says the firm has worked with more than 450,000 Canadians and has more than 300 mortgage experts. Those are nesto's figures, not a count we audited.

nesto.whoItsFor:
nesto fits a borrower who will upload documents, talk to a salaried advisor on the phone or online, and wants the rate visible before a negotiation. The long hold is useful if you are buying on a closing date months away or starting a renewal early. Cash-back is useful only after you compare the rate with and without it. A lower rate with no cash-back often wins. Run both payments in the payment calculator.

Skip nesto if you want a branch, a readvanceable line registered with a bank you already use, or a file its lenders will not take: some alternative-credit, rural, or non-resident cases belong with a specialist such as Home Trust or Equitable Bank, through a broker who actually has those shelves. Confirm your province against the current licence list before you spend an evening on the application.

products.title: nesto-funded mortgage
products.description: A loan nesto originates and services. You should see nesto, or the specific funding entity they name, as the lender on the disclosure. Prepayment, penalty, and portability are whatever that commitment says. Do not import another lender's 20 percent privilege.

products.title: Brokered mortgage
products.description: A loan from a partner, arranged by nesto's licensed brokerage. The partner's penalty clause, charge type, and renewal desk are the ones you will live with. Ask for the lender's name before you waive conditions.

products.title: Fixed and variable five-year terms
products.description: The public scrape we store is concentrated on five-year fixed and five-year variable, split into insured and uninsured. Shorter terms may exist and simply not be in today's file. Match the label. An insured special is not a quote for a 20-percent-down refinance.

products.title: Cash-back option and 150-day hold
products.description: nesto's FAQ says most solutions can hold a rate for 150 days and that a 1 percent cash-back option is available. Confirm both against the term you want. Cash-back can be clawed back if you break early. Ask that question in writing.

nesto.howRatesCompare:
Judge nesto from the cells in the rate block, not from a sentence on this page. When the scrape is healthy you will see a five-year fixed and a five-year variable, each in an insured and an uninsured version. Compare those four, one at a time, with Wealthsimple, True North Mortgage, and the insured and uninsured hubs.

nesto's site sometimes prints a Big Six average beside its own insured special. That average mixes posted and discounted bank rates and is not a promise you will save that gap. A fair comparison is one bank's written special, same term, same default-insurance status. The posted-versus-discounted guide is the warning label on bank advertising.
shoppingTips: Ask whether nesto will be the lender of record or the broker. The penalty clause follows the lender, not the website.
If the file might be CMLS, open that lender's privilege and penalty pages. Ownership by nesto does not merge the contracts.
Price the 1 percent cash-back against the no-cash-back rate on the same term. Use the payment calculator for the five-year interest, then subtract the cash only if you expect to keep the loan.
Write down the hold length and whether one float-down is included. A 150-day hold that cannot drop is less useful in a falling market.
Qualification is still real. High-ratio files follow insurer rules. Use the stress-test qualifier with the contract rate before you rely on a pre-approval.

extraSections.heading: Licences, and why the lender's name is not a detail
extraSections.html:
nesto publishes a jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction licence table. Ontario, Saskatchewan, New Brunswick, and Nova Scotia show numbered brokerage registrations. Nova Scotia also lists a lender licence and an administrator licence. Several other provinces and the territories are named in the footer without a brokerage number on that row. Quebec is explicitly "not applicable" under the distribution statute. None of this is a review of nesto's compliance. It is a map of what they claim they are allowed to do, and it is the reason two nesto clients can have completely different mortgage contracts.

Before you compare a nesto five-year with a bank five-year, get the funding lender, the charge type (standard or collateral), the prepayment percent, and the penalty method. Those four facts decide whether the cheaper rate is the cheaper mortgage. The lender-type guide is the background.

faqs.question: Is nesto a bank?
faqs.answer: No. nesto is a digital mortgage platform. Its licence disclosures show brokerage and administrator registrations, and in Nova Scotia a lender licence as well. Some mortgages are nesto's own. Others are arranged with a partner lender. The commitment says which.

faqs.question: Does nesto guarantee the lowest rate in Canada?
faqs.answer: nesto's "Low Mortgage Rate Guarantee" is its description of showing the lowest applicable rate up front, with salaried advisors. It is not a promise to beat every competitor's quote or to pay you a set amount if they cannot. The rate that matters is the one on the approval, for your term and your insured or uninsured status.

faqs.question: How long will nesto hold a rate?
faqs.answer: nesto's FAQ says a 150-day rate hold is available on most of its solutions, and it contrasts that with a 120-day hold it says is typical elsewhere. Confirm the hold on the product you were offered, including whether the rate can float down once.

faqs.question: Is a nesto mortgage the same as a CMLS mortgage?
faqs.answer: No. nesto acquired CMLS on 20 June 2024. CMLS still lends through the broker channel under the CMLS name, including its Aveo alternative program. Ask which company will be on your mortgage documents.

faqs.question: Which provinces does nesto serve?
faqs.answer: The licence page names brokerage or related registrations across the provinces and territories, with specific numbers in Ontario, Saskatchewan, New Brunswick, and Nova Scotia. Quebec is marked not applicable under the distribution act. Confirm your property's province with nesto before you apply.

faqs.question: Where do today's nesto rates come from?
faqs.answer: From the scrape shown at the top of this page, taken from nesto's public rate pages. We do not type a five-year figure into this answer. If a cell is missing, that term was not in the file.

simplii.name: Simplii Financial
simplii.tagline: CIBC's no-branch division, with a 20 percent privilege and a posted-rate penalty.
simplii.seoDescription: Simplii Financial mortgage rates. Simplii is a division of CIBC, does not offer banking in Quebec, and its standard terms add your discount back when a fixed penalty is calculated.
simplii.heroIntro: Simplii Financial is a division of CIBC, not a standalone bank. The uninsured rows above are the scrape. The contract terms below are from Simplii's own standard mortgage terms.
simplii.overview:
Simplii Financial is a division of CIBC. The standard mortgage terms say so in the footer, and they say the Simplii name and designs are CIBC trademarks. Deposits sit with CIBC. There is no branch network to walk into. You apply and manage the mortgage online or by phone. The same footer states that banking services are not available in Quebec, so a Quebec property is the wrong file for this lender.

The prepayment clause is more specific than a marketing line. On a fixed term of two years or longer, on a variable-rate mortgage, and on an Auto 12 Plus convertible, you may prepay up to 20 percent of the original principal each mortgage year without a charge. An Auto 6 Plus convertible is limited to 10 percent. The prepayment has to fall on a regular payment date, the minimum is $100, and unused room dies at the end of that mortgage year. The privilege does not cover paying the loan off in full, even if you have not used the 20 percent. The property has to be no more than four units, or a single condo, and it cannot be used for business. Separately, Simplii's prepayment-options page says you can increase the payment once each mortgage year by up to 25 percent of the payment you chose at the start or at the last renewal. That increase and the lump sum are different tools. Confirm both are on your offer.

The penalty is where Simplii behaves like its parent. For a fixed term of two years or longer, the charge is the higher of two amounts. The first is three months' interest on the amount you are prepaying, calculated at your contract rate plus any discount you received. The second is an interest-rate differential that also starts from the contract rate plus the discount, and compares that with the interest cost at the rate Simplii posts, on the prepayment date, for a similar closed Simplii mortgage. "Similar" looks at the remaining term, the features, and whether the mortgage is conventional or high-ratio. Adding the discount back, then comparing with a posted rate, is the calculation that makes a big-bank break fee larger than a lender who simply differences your contract rate against today's contract rate. Read how that gap is built before you take a Simplii fixed rate you might not finish.

A variable prepayment charge, on Simplii's public options page, is three months' interest using the CIBC prime rate, not an interest-rate differential. After the fifth year of a term longer than five years, a borrower who is not a corporation can pay the loan out for three months' interest. That cap is the federal rule showing up in the contract. It does not soften years one through five.

simplii.whoItsFor:
Simplii fits someone who already keeps day-to-day banking there, lives outside Quebec, and wants a straightforward closed mortgage with a large annual prepayment. The 20 percent lump sum is real room if your income is lumpy and you will use it. The 25 percent payment increase is a second path if you would rather raise the regular debit than send lump sums.

It is a poor fit if you might sell or refinance in the first five years of a discounted fixed term. The penalty math adds your discount back before it looks at Simplii's posted rate. It is also the wrong door if you want CIBC's Home Power Plan, which is a collateral, readvanceable product sold by CIBC rather than by this no-branch division. And it is unavailable, on Simplii's own terms, for Quebec banking. A high-ratio borrower should still read first-time buyer programs and run the default-insurance calculator. Simplii's current scrape on this site does not include an insured column.

products.title: Fixed term of two years or longer
products.description: Closed fixed rates with a 20 percent annual lump-sum privilege, minimum $100, on a regular payment date, no carry-forward. Breaking it costs the higher of three months' interest at the rate plus your discount, or the posted-rate differential described in the standard terms.

products.title: Variable-rate mortgage
products.description: Same 20 percent lump-sum privilege. A prepayment charge is three months' interest calculated with CIBC prime, according to Simplii's options page. There is no interest-rate differential on that variable charge. Confirm the page still says CIBC prime when you sign.

products.title: Auto 6 Plus and Auto 12 Plus
products.description: Short convertible terms. The standard terms limit the Auto 6 Plus penalty-free lump sum to 10 percent of the original principal. Auto 12 Plus stays at 20 percent. These terms can renew automatically if Simplii does not tell you it will not renew. Read clause 8 before you treat a six-month term as a one-time loan.

products.title: Payment increase
products.description: Once each mortgage year you can raise the regular payment by up to 25 percent of the payment selected when the term started or last renewed. That is separate from the lump sum. It is not available on every vintage. Ask.

simplii.howRatesCompare:
The Simplii rows in our file are uninsured fixed terms from two years through five, plus a five-year variable, when the scrape includes them. There is no insured Simplii column in the current feed. A high-ratio quote has to come from Simplii directly. Do not paste an uninsured cell into an insured comparison.

Put the written Simplii special next to CIBC, Tangerine, and the uninsured hub. Simplii will often look sharper than CIBC's posted rate and closer to other direct digital banks. The fair question is whether you will finish the term. If you will, the harsh penalty is cheap insurance you never collect. If you will not, price the break with Simplii's prepayment calculator before you prefer their rate over a monoline.
shoppingTips: Confirm the property is outside Quebec. Simplii's mortgage terms say banking services are not available there.
Ask which privilege you are getting: 20 percent, or 10 percent on an Auto 6 Plus. Get the 25 percent payment-increase in the same email.

On a fixed quote, ask the advisor to say the penalty uses your rate plus the discount, compared with Simplii's posted rate for a similar product. If they describe a softer method, ask them to point at the clause.
Do not assume a full payout can use the unused 20 percent. The terms say the privilege does not apply to paying the entire principal.
If you want a readvanceable line, you are in the wrong brand. That conversation is CIBC Home Power Plan, with its own charge.

extraSections.heading: Why the discount shows up inside the penalty
extraSections.html:
Suppose Simplii posts 5 percent and offers you 4 percent. The discount is one point. On a break, the standard terms do not difference 4 percent against today's posted rate and stop. They add the one point back, so the interest they treat you as owing is calculated at 5 percent, and they compare that with the posted rate of a similar Simplii mortgage for the time left. The gap is wider than the gap between the rate you pay and the rate a new borrower pays. That is the same family of clause the posted-rate guide warns about, written into a no-branch division of a Big Six bank.

A variable charge avoids that differential and uses three months at CIBC prime. The prime rate can be higher than your discounted variable contract rate, so "three months' interest" is not automatically three months at the rate on your statement. Check the options page and the commitment together.

faqs.question: Is Simplii a separate bank from CIBC?
faqs.answer: No. Simplii Financial is a division of CIBC, and the mortgage terms say the brand is a CIBC trademark. You do not get a Simplii branch. You also do not get a different deposit insurer from CIBC. The mortgage contract is still its own document, with the privileges and penalty written for Simplii products.

faqs.question: Can I get a Simplii mortgage in Quebec?
faqs.answer: Simplii's standard mortgage terms say banking services are not available in Quebec. If the property or the borrower needs a Quebec file, use a lender that actually lends there, such as National Bank or Desjardins, and confirm eligibility with them.

faqs.question: How much can I prepay without a penalty?
faqs.answer: Up to 20 percent of the original principal each mortgage year on a fixed term of two years or longer, on a variable, and on an Auto 12 Plus. Auto 6 Plus is 10 percent. Minimum $100, on a regular payment date, no carry-forward. A full payout does not get to use that privilege. You may also be able to raise the payment by up to 25 percent once a year.

faqs.question: Does Simplii use a posted-rate penalty?
faqs.answer: On fixed terms of two years or longer, yes. The charge is the higher of three months' interest at your rate plus the discount, or an interest-rate differential against the posted rate of a similar closed Simplii mortgage. The discount is added back. That is harsher than a lender who differences the contract rate you actually pay.

faqs.question: What is the variable penalty?
faqs.answer: Simplii's prepayment-options page says a variable prepayment charge is three months' interest, and the rate used is the CIBC prime rate. It is not an interest-rate differential. Confirm the current page before you rely on a blog summary, including this one.

tangerine.name: Tangerine
tangerine.tagline: Scotiabank's separate digital bank, with a 25/25 privilege and its own prime rate.
tangerine.seoDescription: Tangerine mortgage rates from the live scrape. Tangerine Bank is owned by Scotiabank, lends on residential property across Canada, and publishes a 25 percent prepayment privilege.
tangerine.heroIntro: Tangerine Bank is owned by Scotiabank and takes applications online. The uninsured fixed and variable rows above are today's scrape, not a Scotiabank branch special.
tangerine.overview:
Tangerine is a trade name of Tangerine Bank. Tangerine's own pages describe that bank as a wholly owned subsidiary of The Bank of Nova Scotia, and as a CDIC member in its own right. Owning the shares does not make a Tangerine mortgage a Scotiabank STEP component. The prime rate is Tangerine's prime. The HELOC, if you add one, is a Tangerine home equity line. The charge, the privilege, and the renewal offer come from Tangerine.

You do not visit a Tangerine branch, because there isn't a branch network in the usual sense. Applications are online or by phone. The loan-application terms say mortgage and home-equity-line products are available to Canadian residents for residential property in Canada, including the Quebec language clause in those terms. Eligibility still depends on the property, the equity, and Tangerine's credit rules. The property FAQ is blunt about exclusions: residential zoning, up to four units, and no agricultural property, no commercial property, no housing co-operative, no mobile home, and no log cabin. Call them if the building is unusual. Do not assume a cottage or a small mixed-use building will pass.

The prepayment package is the 25/25 that Tangerine spells out in its help pages. Each mortgage year you can raise the regular payment by up to 25 percent of the original payment, and you can make lump sums of up to 25 percent of the original mortgage amount on a scheduled payment date. Accelerated weekly or biweekly payments add roughly an extra month of principal over a year. Skip-a-payment is described for conventional mortgages. Go past the privilege and a charge applies: three months' interest on a variable, and the greater of three months' interest or an interest-rate differential on a fixed. Tangerine's estimate page tells you to phone for the exact figure. Their FAQ also says amortizations are available for up to 25 years. If you need a 30-year amortization, ask whether that sentence still governs your file or whether a newer program has opened. Do not discover it at the notary.

Tangerine sells a home equity line of credit beside the mortgage, at Tangerine prime plus or minus a spread, with no annual fee described on the product page. It is not automatically readvanceable in the STEP sense, and it is not registered as a Scotia collateral plan. The application terms do say cost-of-borrowing disclosure for a real-property loan can arrive when you sign a collateral mortgage agreement or a HELOC agreement, if you did not get it earlier and you consent. Ask whether your Tangerine mortgage will be a collateral charge before you count on an easy assignment at renewal.

Residential property up to four units
uniqueFeatures: CDIC member in its own right

tangerine.whoItsFor:
Tangerine fits a borrower who wants the mortgage, the savings account, and the line in one online bank, and who will use a large prepayment privilege. Twenty-five percent of the original balance is meaningful room on a jumbo loan if you actually have the cash. The HELOC is the tool for smaller, repeating draws, without breaking the mortgage to get at equity.

Look at a branch bank or a broker if the property is a co-op, a farm, a mobile home, or anything Tangerine's FAQ lists as out of scope. Look at a monoline if you want a standard charge and a penalty that is three months' interest on a fixed term too. And do not open a Tangerine application expecting Scotiabank STEP features. They are different contracts inside one corporate family. The fixed-versus-variable guide is the rate-type decision. The penalty method is the other decision.

products.title: Fixed mortgage
products.description: Rate and payment hold for the term. Lump sums up to 25 percent of the original amount, and a payment increase up to 25 percent of the original payment, each mortgage year. A break costs the greater of three months' interest and an interest-rate differential. Ask how Tangerine picks the comparison rate.

products.title: Variable mortgage
products.description: Priced as a spread to Tangerine prime. The help pages say the spread is set for the five-year term while prime can move, and that Tangerine reviews prime on a quarterly cadence even though prime itself can change at any time. A prepayment charge is three months' interest. Payment can change when prime changes. Read the agreement for whether the payment is fixed or floating.

products.title: Home equity line of credit
products.description: A variable line at Tangerine prime plus or minus a factor, described without an annual fee. You can repay and redraw. It does not replace the mortgage penalty if you are paying the mortgage out. The line is unavailable as a workaround for a property type the mortgage FAQ excludes.

products.title: What they will not finance
products.description: Agricultural, commercial, and co-operative property, mobile homes, and log cabins are named exclusions. Everything else still has to meet credit, equity, and maximum-loan rules. Canadian residents, residential property in Canada.

tangerine.howRatesCompare:
Tangerine's scrape on this site is an uninsured shelf: fixed terms from one year out to seven and ten when those rows are published, and a five-year variable. There is no insured Tangerine column in the feed. Compare an uninsured five-year with Simplii, Scotiabank, and the uninsured hub. Do not line an uninsured Tangerine cell up against an insured monoline special and call the monoline cheaper. The products are different.

Tangerine does not hide behind a posted rate the way a branch bank does, which makes the table easier to read and the penalty clause more important. A transparent rate with an interest-rate differential can still be the expensive mortgage if you move in year two. Price that case with the penalty calculator as a sketch, then get Tangerine's number.
shoppingTips: Ask whether the mortgage will be registered as a collateral charge. The application terms contemplate a collateral mortgage agreement. A standard charge is easier to move later.
Write down both halves of 25/25: lump sum measured on the original amount, payment increase measured on the original payment. They are not the same base.
If you need a 30-year amortization, ask before you fall in love with the rate. Tangerine's FAQ has said amortizations go up to 25 years.
Check the property against the exclusion list yourself. A co-op apartment in a city Tangerine otherwise serves is still a no.
Keep STEP and Tangerine apart in the comparison. One is Scotiabank's readvanceable plan. The other is a separate bank's mortgage and HELOC.

extraSections.heading: A subsidiary is not a product match
extraSections.html:
People shop Tangerine because the parent is Scotiabank and then expect STEP, a branch, or Scotia's privilege band. None of those transfer. Tangerine Bank has its own CDIC membership, its own prime, its own 25 percent privilege, and its own home equity line. Scotiabank's collateral-charge warning about closing STEP before a second mortgage is a Scotia document. Ask Tangerine the charge question directly.

The useful comparison is with other no-branch lenders, especially Simplii, and with a brokered monoline on a standard charge. Ownership explains who stands behind the deposits. It does not pick the winner on a five-year fixed. Use the rows above for Tangerine's current uninsured quotes and the lender-type guide for the contract differences.

faqs.question: Is Tangerine the same as Scotiabank?
faqs.answer: Tangerine Bank is a wholly owned subsidiary of The Bank of Nova Scotia, and Tangerine says it is a CDIC member on its own. A Tangerine mortgage is not a Scotia Total Equity Plan mortgage. Rates, prime, prepayment, and the HELOC are Tangerine's.

faqs.question: How much can I prepay?
faqs.answer: Tangerine's help pages describe a 25/25 option each mortgage year: increase the payment by up to 25 percent of the original payment, and make lump sums up to 25 percent of the original mortgage amount on a payment date. Accelerated weekly or biweekly adds about an extra month of payments. Amounts above the privilege can trigger a charge.

faqs.question: What does it cost to break a Tangerine mortgage?
faqs.answer: Variable: three months' interest. Fixed: the greater of three months' interest and an interest-rate differential. Tangerine tells you to use its calculator as an estimate and to call for the actual charge. The comparison rate inside the differential is a question for that call.

faqs.question: Does Tangerine have a HELOC?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tangerine offers a home equity line of credit priced off Tangerine prime, and the product page describes borrowing without an annual fee and without breaking the mortgage. It is still a separate credit agreement. It is not offered as a way around a property type they will not mortgage.

faqs.question: Will Tangerine lend on any home in Canada?
faqs.answer: The application terms say Canadian residents and residential property in Canada, which includes Quebec paperwork in those terms. The property FAQ excludes agricultural and commercial property, co-ops, mobile homes, and log cabins, and it caps eligible property at four units. Credit, equity, and maximum loan size still apply.

faqs.question: Why are Tangerine's rates on this page all uninsured?
faqs.answer: Because that is what the scrape of Tangerine's public rate page contained. We do not fill in an insured column. If you are putting less than 20 percent down, ask Tangerine whether they will do a high-ratio file and at what rate. Until they quote it, it is not a number we have.

wealthsimple.whoItsFor:
Wealthsimple mortgages fit people who want a digital application, are comfortable with a broker shopping multiple lenders rather than a bank branch, and (for cash-back) already use or will open Wealthsimple Chequing. alterna.name: Alterna Bank
alterna.tagline: A Schedule I digital bank owned by the Alterna Savings credit union.
alterna.seoDescription: Alterna Bank mortgage rates. Alterna Bank is owned by Alterna Savings, is OSFI-regulated, and its online mortgages combine a 20 percent annual prepayment cap with no Quebec mortgages.
alterna.heroIntro: The lender in the table is Alterna Bank, a federal bank owned by Alterna Savings and Credit Union Limited. Quebec mortgages are excluded on Alterna's own homebuying page.
alterna.overview:
The rates on this page come from Alterna Bank, not from a generic credit-union rate card. Alterna Bank's 2025 financial statements, issued in March 2026, describe CS Alterna Bank as a Schedule I bank operating under the name Alterna Bank, a CDIC member, regulated by OSFI, and a wholly owned subsidiary of Alterna Savings and Credit Union Limited. Alterna Savings is the ultimate parent. Letters patent date from 2 October 2000. The registered office in those statements is on McRae Avenue in Ottawa. The bank says its business is deposits and loans for clients across Canada. The accessibility plan adds the operating picture: most clients use the website or the app, everyone can use the ATMs, and some services are available at agency branches. Alterna Bank has no dedicated employees. Alterna Savings staff do the work.

That structure is easy to blur. Alterna Savings is an Ontario credit union. Alterna Bank is the federal subsidiary that publishes the mortgage rates we scrape. A membership conversation may still happen because the parent is a credit union and the staff are the credit union's. The mortgage, the CDIC coverage, and the OSFI supervision attach to the bank. Ask which legal name will be on the charge.

The homebuying page says the mortgages are not available for Quebec. It also advertises flexible prepayment on the online mortgages and closing costs covered up to $1,000, with conditions marked on that page. Read the current asterisks. A covered-cost offer is a promotion, not a term of every renewal.

Prepayment is a combined cap, which is the detail people miss. Alterna says that each calendar year you can increase the regular payment by as much as double, and you can make an additional payment of up to 20 percent of the original balance, but the sum of the increase and the lump sums cannot exceed 20 percent of the original principal. Using the payment increase uses up lump-sum room. The renewal page repeats it: closed terms allow an annual prepayment of up to 20 percent, either as one or more prepayments or by increasing payments to not more than twice the original amount. Go past 20 percent and a charge may apply. Mortgages funded before 16 May 2021 can be on an older calculator. If your loan is that old, use the link Alterna provides for the earlier rules rather than the current page.
specialties: Federal bank owned by a credit union
uniqueFeatures: Payment increases and lump sums share one 20 percent pool
Closing-cost offer up to $1,000, conditions on the page
Pre-May 2021 mortgages can use older prepayment rules
Staff are Alterna Savings employees
alterna.whoItsFor:
Alterna Bank fits a borrower outside Quebec who wants a direct online mortgage from a smaller Schedule I bank, with a parent that is a member-owned Ontario credit union. The combined 20 percent room is enough for someone who will either raise the payment or send lump sums, and who understands those two actions draw from the same annual pool.

It is the wrong lender for a Quebec property. It is also a weaker choice if you want the payment doubled and a separate 20 percent lump sum in the same year. Alterna's wording caps the combination. A monoline that offers 15 percent lump sum plus double-up plus a payment increase, as separate privileges, can let you prepay more even when the headline percent looks smaller. Compare the clauses, not the slogans, and use the penalty guide once you know how Alterna calculates a charge above the cap. Their calculator estimates it. The commitment sets it.

products.title: Online closed mortgage
products.description: The homebuying page is aimed at purchases and switches, outside Quebec. Weekly, biweekly, and semi-monthly frequencies are offered as a way to pay faster. The annual cap is 20 percent of original principal across payment increases and lump sums together.

products.title: Insured and uninsured terms in the scrape
products.description: Our file often shows insured fixed and variable terms at the three- and five-year marks, and a longer list of uninsured fixed terms from six months upward, plus uninsured variables. Match the column. An insured Alterna cell is not a quote for a conventional refinance.

products.title: Closing-cost credit
products.description: Alterna advertises closing costs covered up to $1,000 on the online mortgage page, subject to the conditions printed there. Ask what is reimbursed, what the maximum is this month, and whether a switch qualifies. Do not subtract $1,000 from your own estimate until the offer is on the approval.

products.title: Older mortgages
products.description: If the loan was funded before 16 May 2021, Alterna points you to a different prepayment path. Privileges and the charge can differ from the current 20 percent combined cap. Pull the original disclosure before you plan a lump sum.

alterna.howRatesCompare:
Read Alterna's insured cells and uninsured cells as separate products. In the current shape of our feed, insured pricing shows up on a short list of terms and uninsured pricing shows up on a wider set of fixed terms, often at higher rates. That pattern is normal. It is not a reason to average them.

Set an Alterna five-year next to Meridian if you are in Ontario, next to Simplii if you want another no-branch option, and next to the five-year fixed hub. Alterna is a direct lender with a credit-union parent, which puts it in a different bucket from a brokered monoline. The lender-type guide covers that bucket. Because the bank is OSFI-regulated, do not expect a provincial credit-union exception from federal qualification rules on a new uninsured loan.
shoppingTips: Ask for the legal name on the charge: Alterna Bank, not "Alterna" in the abstract. CDIC and OSFI attach to the bank.
Confirm the property is outside Quebec before you collect documents.
Map the 20 percent pool. If you double the payment, ask how much lump-sum room is left that calendar year.
If the mortgage was funded before 16 May 2021, open the older prepayment calculator. The new page is the wrong rule set.
Treat the $1,000 closing-cost offer as conditional. Get it on the commitment if you are counting on it to fund the lawyer.

extraSections.heading: Credit union parent, bank mortgage
extraSections.html:
Alterna Savings and Credit Union Limited owns the bank and employs the people who operate it. Members of the credit union sometimes assume the mortgage is a credit-union loan with provincial deposit insurance and provincial mortgage rules. Alterna Bank's financial statements say otherwise: Schedule I, CDIC, OSFI, loans to clients across Canada, except that the retail mortgage page then carves Quebec out. Both facts can be true. The charter is national. The product is not offered on Quebec mortgages.

When you renew, the offer is Alterna Bank's. Switching away is a new lender's underwriting, plus whatever charge type was registered. Ask at the start whether the charge is conventional or collateral. We did not find a single public Alterna sentence that settles that for every online mortgage, so the honest step is to ask. The switch guide explains why the answer changes the legal bill.

faqs.question: Is Alterna Bank the same as Alterna Savings?
faqs.answer: No. Alterna Bank is a Schedule I bank and a wholly owned subsidiary of Alterna Savings and Credit Union Limited. The bank is a CDIC member regulated by OSFI. The credit union is the parent and, according to Alterna Bank's accessibility plan, supplies the staff. Ask which name will be on your mortgage.

faqs.question: Can I get an Alterna mortgage in Quebec?
faqs.answer: Alterna's homebuying page says its mortgages are not available for Quebec. The bank's financial statements describe clients across Canada. The product restriction is the one that matters for a home loan. Use a lender that will take a Quebec file.

faqs.question: Can I double my payment and still prepay 20 percent?
faqs.answer: Not as two full, separate allowances. Alterna says the payment increase, up to double, and the additional payments together cannot exceed 20 percent of the original principal in a calendar year. One uses the room of the other.

faqs.question: What if my Alterna mortgage started before May 2021?
faqs.answer: Alterna's prepayment calculator tells borrowers funded before 16 May 2021 to use a different path. The privilege and the charge on that older book can differ from the current 20 percent cap. Read the disclosure you signed.

faqs.question: Does Alterna pay my closing costs?
faqs.answer: The homebuying page advertises closing costs covered up to $1,000, with conditions. It is an offer on that page, not a permanent feature of every Alterna mortgage. Confirm the current amount, what it covers, and whether your transaction qualifies.
