firstnational.name: First National Financial
firstnational.tagline: A broker-channel monoline, privately held since October 2025, with a 15 percent privilege and double-up payments.
firstnational.seoDescription: First National mortgage rates from the live scrape. Broker-only single-family lending, 15 percent prepayments, double-up payments, and an IRD tied to First National's replacement rate.
firstnational.heroIntro: First National funds single-family mortgages almost entirely through brokers. The uninsured terms above are the current scrape. Privileges and the penalty come from your mortgage documents, not from this table.
firstnational.overview:
First National Financial LP originates, underwrites, and services prime residential mortgages, both single-family and multi-unit, plus commercial loans. Its parent, First National Financial Corporation, described itself in the second-quarter 2026 MD&A as one of Canada's largest non-bank mortgage originators, with almost $170 billion in mortgages under administration and a top-three share of the broker channel. You do not walk into a First National branch and leave with a mortgage. The annual information form says single-family loans are sourced almost exclusively through independent brokers and the existing customer base. Multi-unit and commercial loans are sourced largely by in-house underwriters.

Ownership changed on 22 October 2025. A plan of arrangement took the common shares private. Birch Hill Equity Partners and Brookfield Asset Management, through an acquisition company, bought the common shares other than those the founders rolled. Stephen Smith and Moray Tawse each kept an indirect stake of about 19 percent, and Birch Hill and Brookfield held the rest, about 62 percent. The company amalgamated and kept the First National name. Preferred shares stayed listed. None of that changes the servicing portal or the broker relationship, but it does retire the idea that First National is still the TSX common-stock story it was for the previous nineteen years.

Day to day, borrowers live in My Mortgage. Prepayment privileges, which First National says are already built in and should be checked against the documents, come in four shapes. You can make accelerated payments that add up to about thirteen months of payments in a year, though not on a monthly frequency. You can pay a lump sum of up to 15 percent of the original balance each anniversary year, all at once or spread across payments, minimum $100. You can double a payment, and the double-up applies to principal and interest, not to tax or insurance add-ons. On a fixed rate only, you can increase the regular payment by up to 15 percent once in an anniversary year, and you cannot stop and restart that increase in the same year. A year runs from the interest-adjustment or renewal anniversary. Unused room does not roll over.

A closed adjustable-rate payout is three months' interest. A closed fixed payout is the greater of three months' interest and an interest-rate differential. First National defines that differential as the gap between your rate and First National's current rate on a replacement mortgage for the time remaining. The prepayment page also says changes in First National posted rates affect IRD calculations. After the fifth anniversary of a term longer than five years, the charge becomes three months' interest. With fewer than three months left, a per-diem charge covers the stub. Paying the loan off can add a discharge administration fee, and a cash-back offer can be clawed back in part. Porting, or having a qualified buyer assume the mortgage, can avoid the charge. Terms apply.
uniqueFeatures: Taken private in October 2025 by Birch Hill, Brookfield, and the founders
IRD uses First National's replacement rate
Payment increase cannot be restarted the same anniversary year
Almost $170 billion under administration as of the 2026 MD&A
firstnational.whoItsFor:
First National fits a borrower who is already using a mortgage broker, wants a prime single-family loan, and cares about a servicing company that is built to administer mortgages rather than to cross-sell a chequing account. The double-up plus the 15 percent lump sum is a practical pair if your income arrives in chunks. Multi-unit owners are in a different lineup, talked through with First National's own commercial staff or a broker who does that book.

Look elsewhere if you want a branch, a readvanceable bank line, or a same-day relationship discount tied to moving your payroll. Also look elsewhere if the file is alternative credit. First National's single-family business is predominantly prime. An early exit from a fixed term still needs an IRD quote, because "monoline" does not mean "three months' interest on every product." The lender-type guide is the map.

products.title: Single-family residential
products.description: Prime mortgages arranged by a broker. The public rate page we scrape has been an uninsured fixed list across several terms, including seven- and ten-year rows when they are published. Insured pricing may exist and not be in this feed. Ask the broker which column your down payment lands in.

products.title: Prepayment set
products.description: Accelerated payments, 15 percent lump sum, double-up, and a fixed-only 15 percent payment increase. The increase, once set, waits until the next anniversary to be changed again. Minimum lump sum is $100. Privileges reset on the mortgage anniversary, not on 1 January.

products.title: Port or assumption
products.description: First National says a qualified assumption or a port to a new home may avoid the prepayment charge. Qualification and conditions apply. A port that needs extra money is a new slice at a new rate. Get the blend, if one is offered, in numbers.

products.title: Multi-unit and commercial
products.description: A separate origination path, largely through First National's own underwriters. A 2026 commercial note said the firm was also brokering conventional financing alongside its insured multi-unit lending. Those rates are not the single-family cells on this page.

firstnational.howRatesCompare:
Treat the First National block as broker-channel uninsured fixed pricing unless an insured or variable row actually appears. Compare a five-year cell with other monolines and with a bank special on the uninsured hub, same term. First National's rate is often the reason a broker brings them into a prime file. The privilege set and the IRD are the reason to keep reading after the rate looks good.

Posted-rate movement changes the IRD even when your contract rate does not. That link is spelled out on First National's charge page. If you might sell before maturity, price the break on a few rate scenarios, not on today's calm market. The posted-versus-discounted guide explains the mechanism. First National's replacement rate is their rate, not a Big Six posted rate, which is already a different comparison from Simplii or Scotiabank.
shoppingTips: Get the broker to name the privileges on your commitment: 15 percent lump sum, double-up, and whether the 15 percent payment increase applies. Fixed only, for that last one.
Ask whether the charge on title will be a standard charge that another lender can take by assignment at renewal. Do not assume every monoline file is standard.
If the term is longer than five years, remember the penalty becomes three months' interest after the fifth anniversary. That can make a seven- or ten-year term less frightening in the back half.
Cash-back, if it was used to win the deal, can be partly repayable on an early payout. Ask for the schedule.
Renewal is a conversation with First National through My Mortgage and with your broker. The renewal playbook is the timeline. You are not walking into a branch offer.

extraSections.heading: What private ownership does, and does not, change
extraSections.html:
The October 2025 arrangement ended public trading in First National common shares. Founders Smith and Tawse kept minority indirect stakes. Birch Hill and Brookfield hold the majority. Preferred shares remained outstanding and listed. Servicing stayed at First National. For a borrower, the practical point is continuity of the company that collects the payment and calculates the penalty, not a new brand and not a bank conversion.

The contractual point that was true before the deal is still the one to underwrite: closed fixed breaks use the greater of three months' interest and an IRD against First National's replacement rate, and posted-rate changes move that IRD. Log into My Mortgage or call the number on your annual statement for the figure. Our table will not compute it.

faqs.question: Can I get a First National mortgage without a broker?
faqs.answer: Single-family mortgages are sourced almost exclusively through brokers and from First National's existing customers. There is no retail branch network for a new purchase. If you already have a First National mortgage, My Mortgage and their service line are how you manage it.

faqs.question: What are the prepayment options?
faqs.answer: First National describes a 15 percent lump sum each anniversary year, minimum $100, a double-up of principal and interest, accelerated payments that are not available on monthly frequency, and a 15 percent payment increase that applies to fixed-rate mortgages only and can be set once per anniversary year. Check your documents. Not every privilege is on every product.

faqs.question: How is the fixed penalty calculated?
faqs.answer: The greater of three months' interest and an interest-rate differential. First National defines the differential as the difference between your rate and its current rate on a replacement mortgage for the remaining term, and it says posted-rate changes affect the calculation. After five years on a longer term, the charge is three months' interest.

faqs.question: Is First National still a public company?
faqs.answer: Common shares were acquired on 22 October 2025 by a vehicle controlled by Birch Hill and Brookfield, with founders Stephen Smith and Moray Tawse keeping indirect minority interests. The operating name stayed First National. Preferred shares continued to be listed. The mortgage you hold is still a First National mortgage.

faqs.question: Can I move a First National mortgage to a new house?
faqs.answer: First National says a port, or an assumption by a buyer who qualifies, may avoid the prepayment charge. Conditions and qualification apply. Extra funds for a more expensive house are priced separately. Ask the broker to model the port before you firm up a purchase.

manulife.name: Manulife Bank
manulife.tagline: All-in-one banking that puts your mortgage to work.
manulife.seoTitle: Manulife Bank Mortgage Rates | Manulife One & Posted 2026
manulife.seoDescription: Compare Manulife Bank mortgage rates and Manulife One. See posted fixed and variable offers plus the all-in-one account, then check today's rates.
manulife.overview:
Manulife Bank is a Schedule I Canadian bank and a subsidiary of Manulife Financial. It is not a mortgage-only monoline. The distinctive product is Manulife One: an all-in-one account that can combine a mortgage, a line of credit, and day-to-day deposits so interest is charged on the net borrowed balance after you deposit income. Manulife also sells more conventional Manulife Bank Select fixed and variable mortgages for borrowers who want a standard closed term without operating their chequing account inside the mortgage.

Shop Manulife if the all-in-one structure matches how you actually hold cash. If you only want the lowest 5-year sticker rate and will keep a separate chequing account at another bank, start with the live rates on this page and still compare 5-year fixed offers from other lenders. For a different all-in-one style product, see Scotiabank's STEP.
uniqueFeatures: Manulife One: mortgage + banking combined
Income deposited against mortgage balance
Interest savings tracking
Flexible access to home equity
Digital account management
manulife.whoItsFor:
Manulife One is built for people who will park paycheques, savings, and idle cash in the same account as the mortgage. Interest is calculated on the outstanding net balance, so a large deposit can cut interest in a way a conventional closed mortgage cannot. Households with lumpy income (bonuses, commission, or a sale proceeds parked temporarily) sometimes use that feature on purpose.

Skip One if you spend down to a low balance every month, want the simplest possible mortgage, or dislike mixing daily banking with your home loan. In that case look at Manulife Bank Select or another conventional lender. Manulife Bank is OSFI-regulated, so new purchases and refinances still need to pass the mortgage stress test.

products.title: Manulife One (all-in-one)
products.description: A readvanceable account: deposits reduce the balance that interest is charged on; you can hold variable and, depending on the setup, fixed-rate sub-accounts. Savings come from cash behaviour, not from a magic rate. Fees, sub-account rules, and the base rate are set by Manulife—read the current product page rather than old blog math.

products.title: Manulife Bank Select (conventional)
products.description: Standard closed fixed and variable mortgages if you want a familiar term, payment, and separate chequing account. Compare these first if you are rate-shopping against banks and monolines on a like-for-like 5-year closed product.

products.title: Variable and prime-linked options
products.description: Variable Select and One's base/variable components move with Manulife Bank's prime or base rate, not with a rate you lock for five years. Qualification still uses the stress-test rate, which is higher than the contract rate.

products.title: Home equity access
products.description: One's line-of-credit behaviour is the main way Manulife packages re-borrowing. Conventional HELOC-style access still has combined LTV limits. It is not a substitute for a refinance calculator if you are debt-consolidating a different lender.

manulife.howRatesCompare:
Manulife publishes posted tables and separate special or high-ratio offers. The figures in the cards above come from our feed—use them instead of any rate written in this article. Posted Select rates are often higher than the specials; One's headline savings are partly behavioural (cash sitting against the balance) and partly the contract rate on each sub-account.

On a straight 5-year closed comparison, Manulife is not automatically cheaper than a monoline. Where One can win is total interest over a few years if you genuinely keep a high average deposit. Where it can lose is if the contract rate is higher and your operating balance is thin. Compare insured vs uninsured lines in the matrix, then check variable and insured hubs for context.
shoppingTips: Decide first: Manulife One versus a conventional Select mortgage. Mixing the sales pitch from one product with the rate from the other is how people mis-shop this lender.
Ask for the current Manulife One base rate, any fixed sub-account rates, account fees, and how interest is calculated day-to-day—then model your real average balance, not a best-case month.
If you only want a closed 5-year, compare Select (or another lender) on term, insured vs uninsured, and prepayment penalties. Do not assume One is 'always less interest.'
Treat special 'as low as' rates as offer-sheet items with conditions (new clients, high-ratio, term). Match them to the same row in the table on this page.
Manulife Bank still stress-tests new originations. A One application is not a bypass of GDS/TDS.
If you like the all-in-one idea but want a bank you already use, compare the structure to Scotiabank STEP rather than comparing brand slogans.

faqs.question: What is Manulife One?
faqs.answer: Manulife One is an all-in-one banking and mortgage account. Deposits sit against the borrowed balance so you pay interest on the net amount, and you can usually access available credit without opening a separate HELOC application. It is more flexible than a simple closed mortgage and requires more discipline. It is optional; Manulife also offers conventional Select mortgages.

faqs.question: How does Manulife One reduce interest?
faqs.answer: Interest is charged on the outstanding net balance after deposits. A paycheque that sits in the account for two weeks before bills go out reduces interest for those days. If the account is emptied quickly, the benefit shrinks. The contract rate on each sub-account still matters; cash behaviour cannot fix a badly priced rate.

faqs.question: Does Manulife Bank offer ordinary fixed and variable mortgages?
faqs.answer: Yes. Manulife Bank Select is the conventional closed-mortgage lineup. Use that comparison if you want a standard term and payment. Use the rate table on this page for current Select and related figures from our feed.

faqs.question: Is Manulife Bank a real bank?
faqs.answer: Yes. Manulife Bank of Canada is a Schedule I bank regulated by OSFI, separate from Manulife's insurance business even though it is part of the same group. Deposits are eligible for CDIC coverage within CDIC rules. A Manulife One account is still a mortgage product with credit approval, not an investment return.

faqs.question: Who should not choose Manulife One?
faqs.answer: Borrowers who keep almost no cash in the account, who want the lowest possible 5-year closed rate from a brokered monoline, or who prefer not to mix daily spending with their mortgage. Also anyone who would fail the stress test—One does not waive federal qualification on a new purchase or refinance.

faqs.question: Are Manulife's advertised rates the same as posted rates?
faqs.answer: Not always. Manulife shows posted tables and promotional or high-ratio specials with conditions. Compare the specific product (One vs Select, fixed vs variable, insured vs uninsured) to the live matrix on this page. We do not invent a 'today's best Manulife rate' in this article.

laurentian.name: Laurentian Bank
laurentian.tagline: A Quebec Schedule I bank whose retail book was agreed to be sold, and had not closed as of August 2026.
laurentian.seoDescription: Laurentian Bank mortgage rates from the live scrape, the 15/15 prepayment, and the December 2025 deals with National Bank and Fairstone that Laurentian still expected to close in late 2026.
laurentian.heroIntro: Laurentian Bank still publishes mortgage rates. Its August 2026 quarterly report said the sale of the retail book had not closed. Confirm who would fund a new loan before you apply.
laurentian.overview:
Laurentian Bank of Canada is a Schedule I bank based in Montreal, with a bilingual retail history in Quebec and Ontario. Fixed terms on its site run from a closed six months through ten years, plus open terms of six months and one year. Variable terms are described as three- or five-year closed, convertible to a fixed term at least as long as what remains. A fixed pre-approval can hold a rate for up to 120 days. Payments can be monthly, month-end, biweekly, or weekly, with accelerated options on the fixed product.

The fixed prepayment option is branded 15/15. You can make additional payments up to 15 percent of the original loan once a year, and you can increase the payment by up to 15 percent once a year. Prepayments go to principal. The variable page states the 15 percent additional-payment privilege and the convertibility. Anything above the privilege can cost a penalty. Laurentian says the penalty method is the one in the latest Cost of Borrowing Disclosure Statement from the last issue, renewal, or refinance. There is a mortgage penalty and, separately, a promotion penalty if a promotion agreement applies. The online calculator estimates the mortgage penalty and says it does not include the promotion penalty. It also cannot estimate a penalty for a property with six or more units, or for an adjustable-rate mortgage. If your loan is one of those, the calculator's silence is not a zero.

The ownership story is the part that is in motion. On 2 December 2025 Laurentian announced two transactions with National Bank of Canada: a sale of the retail and SME banking portfolios, which includes the residential mortgage relationship, and a separate sale of the syndicated loan portfolio. The same announcement had Fairstone Bank of Canada acquiring all of Laurentian's common shares. Shareholders approved the Fairstone acquisition on 5 February 2026. The syndicated-loan sale closed on 17 February 2026 and was not conditional on the retail sale. By 28 August 2026, Laurentian's third-quarter report said the Competition Bureau had finished its review, the Minister of Finance had approved the share acquisition, OSFI approvals were in hand, and the parties still expected the remaining transactions to close by late 2026, subject to conditions and integration work. This page was written against that August report. It cannot tell you whether closing happened after 28 August 2026. If you are applying now, ask Laurentian whether it is still originating residential mortgages and which institution would service the loan after closing. If you already have a Laurentian mortgage, keep paying it and ask who the servicer will be. Do not assume the rate on this scrape is an offer National Bank or Fairstone has adopted.

laurentian.whoItsFor:
Until the retail transaction closes, Laurentian is still the bank that published these rates and still the name on existing mortgage documents. A borrower who wants a bilingual advisor in Quebec, a 15/15 privilege, and a convertible variable may still be talking to Laurentian. The sensible borrower also asks what happens to the loan when National Bank takes the retail portfolio and Fairstone takes the shares.

If you need certainty about who will renew you in three years, a lender whose ownership is not in a signed but unclosed sale is the calmer choice. National Bank and Desjardins are the obvious Quebec comparisons, and neither comparison should ignore the penalty clause. Laurentian has not, on the pages we reviewed, published a simple "greater of three months or IRD" sentence. The disclosure statement is the source. Use the switch guide if you would rather leave at maturity than guess about the new owner.

products.title: Closed fixed, six months to ten years
products.description: Set payment for the term. The 15/15 option is an extra payment up to 15 percent of the original amount once a year, and a payment increase of up to 15 percent once a year. Open fixed terms of six months and one year exist for borrowers who need an exit.

products.title: Closed variable, three or five years
products.description: Rate moves with Laurentian prime. Payments are described as variable. You can convert to a closed fixed term of equal or longer remaining length. Additional payments up to 15 percent of the original amount once a year. The penalty calculator does not estimate adjustable-rate breaks.

products.title: Pre-approval hold
products.description: Laurentian's fixed-rate page says a pre-approval can hold a rate for up to 120 days. That hold is not a promise the retail sale will still be open on your closing date. Ask what happens to an approval if the portfolio moves before you fund.

products.title: Existing customers during the sale
products.description: The syndicated-loan portfolio already moved to National Bank in February 2026. The retail and SME portfolios, including ordinary residential mortgages, were still expected to move later. Your payment instructions stay valid until Laurentian or the buyer tells you otherwise.

laurentian.howRatesCompare:
The Laurentian scrape we store is a ladder of uninsured fixed terms, from six months through ten years, with no variable row in the current file. A blank variable cell means we did not capture a variable special. It does not mean Laurentian has stopped offering the three- and five-year variable described on its product page.

Line a five-year fixed cell up with National Bank and Desjardins on the uninsured hub. Given the pending sale, a lower Laurentian rate is only attractive if you know who is funding it and who will answer the phone at renewal. The renewal playbook is worth reading even on a new purchase, because the servicer may change before the first term ends.
shoppingTips: Ask whether Laurentian is still originating the mortgage you want, and which institution will own and service it if the retail sale has closed or closes before funding.
Get the 15/15 privilege and the penalty method off the Cost of Borrowing Disclosure Statement, not off a general description.
If a promotion or cash incentive is attached, ask about the separate promotion penalty. The public calculator skips it.
Convertible variable is useful only if you know the fixed term you can convert into and whether the conversion is free. Ask.
Do not treat a 120-day rate hold as protection against the portfolio sale. Ask what the hold becomes if the loan is transferred.

extraSections.heading: What had actually closed by August 2026
extraSections.html:
Two deals are easy to mash together. The syndicated-loan sale to National Bank closed on 17 February 2026. Laurentian received cash, National Bank assumed certain liabilities, and that closing did not depend on the retail sale. The retail and SME portfolio sale to National Bank, and Fairstone's purchase of the common shares, had shareholder approval, Competition Bureau clearance, ministerial approval, and OSFI approval by the summer, and Laurentian's 28 August 2026 report still put closing in late 2026.

Residential mortgage customers are in the retail transaction, not in the syndicated-loan transaction. Until you receive a notice, Laurentian is the servicer. After a notice, follow the payment instructions in that notice. Rate shopping on this page does not move your loan.

faqs.question: Is Laurentian Bank being sold?
faqs.answer: On 2 December 2025 Laurentian agreed that National Bank would buy the retail and SME portfolios and the syndicated loans, and that Fairstone Bank would buy the common shares. The syndicated-loan sale closed on 17 February 2026. As of the 28 August 2026 quarterly report, the retail sale and the share sale were still expected to close by late 2026. Check with the bank for anything that happened after that report.

faqs.question: Should I apply for a new Laurentian mortgage?
faqs.answer: Only after Laurentian confirms it is still funding that product and tells you who would service it if the retail portfolio has moved or is about to. A rate on a public page is not a promise from National Bank or Fairstone.

faqs.question: What is the 15/15 option?
faqs.answer: On a closed fixed mortgage, Laurentian says you can repay up to 15 percent of the original amount once a year and increase the payment by up to 15 percent once a year. Prepayments reduce principal. The variable page states the 15 percent additional-payment privilege. Going beyond the privilege can trigger the penalty in your disclosure statement.

faqs.question: Can I convert a variable mortgage to fixed?
faqs.answer: Laurentian says the closed variable is convertible to a fixed closed term that is the same length or longer than the remaining term. Ask whether the conversion itself has a charge, and what fixed rate you would receive. Do not assume it is today's special.

faqs.question: Why might the penalty calculator refuse my loan?
faqs.answer: Laurentian says the calculator cannot estimate a penalty if the property has six or more units, or if the mortgage is adjustable-rate. It also leaves out any promotion penalty. The Cost of Borrowing Disclosure Statement is the document that actually governs.

butlermortgage.name: Butler Mortgage
butlermortgage.tagline: An Ontario brokerage that shops other lenders and posts the rates on its own site.
butlermortgage.seoDescription: Butler Mortgage rates as labelled Insured on this site. Butler is an Ontario brokerage shopping other lenders, with its own beat-or-$500 rate promise. Confirm the funding lender.
butlermortgage.heroIntro: Butler Mortgage is a brokerage, head office in Etobicoke. Every Butler row on this site is labelled Insured. That is how we file their published sheet. Ask Butler which lender would fund you.
butlermortgage.overview:
Butler Mortgage Inc. is an Ontario mortgage brokerage, not a bank and not a monoline that keeps your loan on its own balance sheet. The about page says the firm shops a network of lenders and that the consultant is paid by the lender when the mortgage funds. The rate page says they track publicly advertised fixed rates from more than 350 prime lenders and use volume to buy the rate down. The head office address they publish is 5397 Eglinton Avenue West, Suite 108, Toronto. Their marketing is aimed at Ontario purchases, renewals, refinances, and construction. If the property is in another province, do not assume this rate card travels. Ask.

The rate promise is specific, and it is theirs, not ours. Butler says that if you find a lower rate they will beat it or pay $500 when the Butler mortgage closes, and that the rate they offer sits in the best 1 percent of rates in Canada. An after-approval version says that if another lender advertises a rate more than a tenth of a point lower and your lender will not match it, you can switch at no cost, and that they will also check for a cut before closing. Read the current page for the conditions. A guarantee with a definition of "similar mortgage" is a contract. A slogan is not. This website does not join that promise. The figures in the table are a scrape of what Butler posted.

On this site, Butler rows are always labelled Insured. That is a standing convention of our rate file, matching the high-ratio sheet Butler features (their Toronto page marks several cells as high-ratio). It does not mean every borrower who calls Butler must take an insured mortgage, and it does not mean a conventional quote will match the cell. Butler's own FAQ describes a high-ratio mortgage as a loan above roughly three-quarters of value, with default insurance, and notes that a lender can still ask for insurance in some cases even with a larger down payment. If you are putting 20 percent or more down, ask for the conventional rate separately. Do not subtract the insured cell from a bank's uninsured cell and call the difference your savings.

Because Butler is the broker, the prepayment privilege, the penalty, the port, and the charge type belong to the lender that funds the file. Those can be a monoline's 15 or 20 percent and an IRD, or a credit union's clause, or something narrower. Butler's site tells you the rate is not a stripped "no frills" product. Take that as a claim to test. Ask which lender, which privilege, and which penalty method are attached to the rate in the table. The penalty guide is how you compare the answers.

butlermortgage.whoItsFor:
Butler fits an Ontario borrower who wants a brokerage to put a rate on the table first, including a high-ratio purchase, and who will still demand the lender's name. Their site also speaks to self-employed borrowers and to people who do not want a branch negotiation. That is a fit when the file is document-heavy and a salaried-bank worksheet is the wrong shape.

It is a poor fit if you need the mortgage held by a specific bank, if the property is outside the provinces they will actually broker, or if you are comparing their insured cell with your uninsured renewal. A straight switch at maturity is often uninsured. Using an insured rate as the benchmark will make every bank look expensive. Read the switch guide and ask Butler for a quote on the same balance, amortization, and insurance status as the mortgage you already have.

products.title: Published high-ratio sheet
products.description: The page we scrape lists fixed terms from six months through ten years and a couple of variable terms, under the Butler name. We label every one of those rows Insured. Treat them as high-ratio indications until Butler confirms the lender and the insurance status in writing.

products.title: The mortgage you actually sign
products.description: Funded by one of the lenders Butler places with. That lender's prepayment, penalty, portability, and renewal process are the product. Butler's job is the advice and the placement. Ask for the lender's standard charge or collateral charge before you waive conditions.

products.title: Self-employed and stated-income style files
products.description: Butler's site says it has options when banks stall on self-employed income, including lower-documentation paths. Those products are priced and qualified by the lender who offers them, often at a higher rate or a fee. Get the lender, the fee, and the beacon expectation. Do not assume the insured special in the table is the rate for that file.

products.title: Rate promise
products.description: Butler's page says they will beat a lower qualifying rate or pay $500 at closing, and that after approval they watch for a competitor rate more than 0.10 percentage points lower. Conditions live on their site. Our table is not an offer under that promise.

butlermortgage.howRatesCompare:
Read the Butler block as an insured comparison only. The terms in our feed run from a very short fixed, through the five-year fixed and variable that brokerages advertise hardest, out to seven- and ten-year fixed. There is no uninsured Butler column, because we do not relabel these rows.

Put the five-year insured cell beside nesto, True North, and the insured hub. Ignore Butler's older website illustrations that compare a 2017 Big Six average with a payment on a $300,000 mortgage. Those examples are historical marketing. Today's number is the cell above, and the lender behind it still has to be named. A tenth of a point against First National or another monoline is only meaningful once the privileges match.
shoppingTips: Ask which lender funds the rate you were shown, and whether that rate is high-ratio insured. On this site the label is Insured either way.
If your down payment is 20 percent or more, ask for a separate conventional quote. Do not reuse the insured cell.
Get the privilege, the penalty method, and the charge type from that lender's commitment. Butler does not replace those clauses.
If you plan to rely on the $500 promise, save the competitor's written offer and Butler's current conditions. Verbal rate-shopping rarely qualifies.
Outside Ontario, confirm they can broker the property. The public rate page is an Ontario page.

extraSections.heading: Why this site refuses to show a Butler uninsured rate
extraSections.html:
Butler publishes a rate table under its own name. The underlying loans are someone else's. Mixing insured and uninsured quotes in one column would make the brokerage look cheaper than a bank on a comparison the borrower cannot actually have. So the overview table, the filters, and this page mark Butler as Insured. That keeps a high-ratio shopper honest and stops an uninsured renewal from being benchmarked against the wrong product.

You can still ask Butler for a conventional mortgage. If they quote one, it is a different rate, from a named lender, and it is not a number we have scraped into an uninsured cell. Default insurance premiums, when the loan is high-ratio, are a separate cost. Estimate them with the insurance calculator and read first-time buyer programs if that is your purchase.

faqs.question: Is Butler Mortgage a lender?
faqs.answer: Butler Mortgage Inc. describes itself as a brokerage that shops other lenders. The company you pay for the next five years is the lender named on the commitment. Butler is paid by that lender when the mortgage funds. Ask for the lender's name before you compare penalties or privileges.

faqs.question: Why does every Butler rate on this site say Insured?
faqs.answer: Because that is our labelling rule for Butler's published sheet, which features high-ratio pricing. It keeps those rows out of uninsured comparisons. It does not stop Butler from arranging a conventional mortgage. A conventional quote will not appear in an uninsured column here until we have a separate scrape, which we do not.

faqs.question: Does Butler guarantee the lowest rate?
faqs.answer: Butler's own page says they will beat a lower rate or pay $500 at closing, and that they aim for the best 1 percent of rates. Conditions are theirs. This website scrapes the posted figures and does not promise to match, beat, or pay that $500.

faqs.question: Can I use a Butler rate to judge my renewal?
faqs.answer: Only if the renewal is an insured mortgage with the same term. Many renewals are uninsured. Comparing your bank's uninsured offer with Butler's insured cell flatters the insured cell. Ask for a quote on your actual balance, remaining amortization, and insurance status.

faqs.question: Who sets the prepayment penalty?
faqs.answer: The funding lender. It might be three months' interest, an interest-rate differential, or a mix. Butler's statement that the rates are full-featured is a starting point. The commitment is the proof. Read the penalty guide so you know which question to ask.

cmls.name: CMLS Financial
cmls.tagline: A broker-channel lender nesto has owned since June 2024, with a prime shelf and an Aveo alternative shelf.
cmls.seoDescription: CMLS mortgage rates from the live scrape. CMLS lends through brokers, allows a 20 percent annual prepayment on its residential FAQ, and runs the Aveo alternative program beside its prime loans.
cmls.heroIntro: CMLS Financial lends through mortgage brokers. nesto has owned it since 20 June 2024. The rates above are the CMLS residential scrape, not Aveo's alternative sheet.
cmls.overview:
CMLS Financial is a Canadian mortgage company that originates residential, multi-unit, and commercial loans and services a large third-party book. You get a CMLS residential mortgage through a broker, not through a branch. CMLS's own FAQ points borrowers at "a CMLS affiliate mortgage broker" for the product choice. Broker materials list an Ontario mortgage brokerage licence, FSRA 11749, and a mortgage administrator licence, FSRA 11689. Those numbers are about the brokerage entity that distributes, not a promise that every province uses the same licence. Ask the broker who will be named on the charge in your province.

On 20 June 2024, nesto Inc. acquired CMLS and its affiliates. A Morningstar DBRS release that CMLS hosts says CMLS did not expect material changes to commercial servicing because of that ownership. The brands stayed distinct. A nesto.ca application is not a CMLS funding. If your broker says "it's all the same company now," ask for the legal name on the commitment anyway. Servicing, prepayment, and the penalty follow that name.

The residential FAQ states the prime-side privilege in one place: on both fixed and adjustable mortgages you can prepay up to 20 percent of the original principal each year, measured from the anniversary, minimum $100, and you can increase payments by up to 20 percent of the original registered amount each anniversary year. CMLS does not, on that FAQ, spell out the break fee. Do not borrow First National's IRD language or a bank's posted-rate language and paste it onto CMLS. Ask the broker for the clause. Porting and blend-and-extend, if you need them, are also commitment items, not FAQ items.

Aveo is the other shelf, and it is not hidden. CMLS describes Aveo as the program for borrowers whose credit, income, or property fall outside mainstream boxes. A broker kit for Aveo residential, marked around mid-2025, limits many files to British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, and Ontario, with one- to three-year closed terms, a beacon floor, a 20 percent lump sum that does not carry forward and is unavailable on a one-year term, and an early-payout charge of 3 percent, then 2 percent, then 1 percent of the principal being prepaid, by year. Aveo+, a July 2026 broker sheet, is a further step out: higher lender fee, no stated GDS/TDS in the usual sense, amortization out to 40 years or interest-only, and fully open 90 days after the interest adjustment date, with Quebec excluded. Those sheets are written for brokers and change. They are not the rates in the table above. If your file is Aveo, the rate and the fee come from the broker's current grid.

uniqueFeatures: Anniversary-year 20 percent lump sum, minimum $100
Aveo early payout quoted as 3, 2, then 1 percent by year
Aveo+ open after 90 days, Quebec excluded on that sheet

cmls.whoItsFor:
CMLS prime fits a borrower whose broker wants a mainstream insured or uninsured loan with a 20 percent privilege and is willing to read the penalty clause before funding. It also fits an investor or a small multi-unit owner when the broker actually has access to that CMLS desk. The commercial book is a different conversation from the single-family rate page.

Aveo fits a borrower a bank has declined for income, credit, or property reasons, who can live with a shorter term, a lender fee, and a percent-of-balance payout schedule instead of an IRD. It does not fit someone who only wanted the lowest insured five-year in the table and did not notice the file was being slotted into alternative. If the broker cannot explain which shelf you are on, stop. The lender-type guide separates prime monolines from alternative lenders. CMLS runs both.

products.title: Prime residential
products.description: Fixed and adjustable mortgages through brokers. The FAQ privilege is 20 percent of original principal per anniversary year, minimum $100, plus a payment increase of up to 20 percent. The scrape on this page mixes insured fixed terms, some longer insured terms at much higher rates, an insured variable, and uninsured fixed terms. Ask which of those cells is a special and which is a posted or niche term.

products.title: Aveo
products.description: Alternative, fully income-qualified files on the broker kit: shorter closed terms, geographic limits, a 20 percent lump sum on terms longer than a year, and a payout charge that steps down by year (3 percent, 2 percent, 1 percent on the kit we reviewed). A commitment fee is part of the pricing. The public rate table is not this grid.

products.title: Aveo+
products.description: A further alternative sheet: open after 90 days, prepayment described as 20/20 and then uncapped, no conventional stress-test line on the sheet, longer amortization or interest-only, and an exclusion for Quebec. Beacon, loan size, and loan-to-value caps are on the current broker sheet. Treat any summary, including this one, as stale until the broker reprints it.

products.title: Commercial and multi-unit
products.description: CMLS services a large multi-family and commercial portfolio, including CMHC-related work. Those loans are not priced off the residential cells above. A residential prepayment sentence does not govern a construction or apartment facility.

cmls.howRatesCompare:
Use the CMLS block for prime residential comparisons only. Insured and uninsured fixed rows both appear in our feed, and the longer insured terms can look nothing like the five-year special. Do not average a ten-year cell with a five-year cell. Put the five-year insured figure, if it is there, against First National, RFA, and the insured hub. Put the uninsured five-year against the uninsured hub.

Aveo will not win that comparison, and it is not supposed to. You are paying for a file a prime lender declined. Compare Aveo's rate plus the lender fee plus the stepped payout charge with another alternative quote, such as Equitable Bank or Home Trust, on the same beacon, the same loan-to-value, and the same term. The refinance calculator is where a one-point fee belongs, next to the rate, not ignored.
shoppingTips: Ask the broker: prime CMLS, Aveo, or Aveo+. The privilege and the payout charge are different products.
On a prime file, get the penalty clause. The FAQ gives the 20 percent privilege and does not define the IRD.
On Aveo, ask for the current year-by-year payout percent and the commitment fee. A kit from last year is not a quote.
Confirm the province. Aveo marketing we reviewed was not national, and Aveo+ excluded Quebec.
If the broker also shops nesto, you are looking at two brands. Pick the one whose name will be on the mortgage.

extraSections.heading: Prime privilege versus alternative payout
extraSections.html:
A 20 percent privilege on a prime CMLS mortgage is there so you can pay the loan down. The penalty for leaving early is a separate sentence you still need to read. On Aveo, the kit we reviewed replaces the usual IRD conversation with a percent of the principal being prepaid: 3 percent in year one, 2 percent in year two, 1 percent in year three, and the 20 percent lump sum is unavailable on a one-year term. Aveo+ then flips the exit: fully open after 90 days. Those are three different promises. A borrower who compares only the rate in our table is comparing the prime shelf, because that is what CMLS publishes on the residential rate page we scrape.

Ownership by nesto does not merge the promises. nesto's 150-day hold and cash-back language live on nesto's FAQ. CMLS's anniversary-year privilege lives on CMLS's FAQ. Quote the document that matches the logo on your disclosure.

faqs.question: Do I need a broker for CMLS?
faqs.answer: Yes for a new residential mortgage. CMLS distributes through brokers and tells borrowers to work with a CMLS-affiliated broker. There is no branch application. Existing borrowers deal with CMLS servicing for payments and payouts.

faqs.question: Is CMLS the same as nesto?
faqs.answer: nesto Inc. acquired CMLS and its affiliates on 20 June 2024. CMLS still originates and services under the CMLS name, including Aveo. A mortgage arranged on nesto.ca can be a different lender of record. Read the commitment.

faqs.question: How much can I prepay on a CMLS residential mortgage?
faqs.answer: The residential FAQ says up to 20 percent of the original principal each anniversary year, minimum $100, on fixed and adjustable mortgages, and a payment increase of up to 20 percent of the original registered amount. Confirm the FAQ still matches your commitment. Alternative Aveo terms can differ, including no lump-sum privilege on a one-year term.

faqs.question: What is Aveo?
faqs.answer: Aveo is CMLS's alternative mortgage program for files that do not fit prime rules. Broker kits describe shorter terms, fees, geographic limits, and an early-payout charge that steps down by year. Aveo+ is a further program that the July 2026 sheet described as open after 90 days and unavailable in Quebec. Your broker's current sheet controls.

faqs.question: Why do some CMLS terms in the table look much higher?
faqs.answer: The scrape includes whatever CMLS posted, and longer insured terms have come through at rates far above the five-year special. Those cells are real postings, not a five-year quote. Compare term with term. If a cell looks like a niche or posted rate, ask the broker for the special on the term you actually want.

rfa.name: RFA
rfa.tagline: Two lenders under one broker-facing roof: RFA Mortgage Corporation for prime, RFA Bank for alternative.
rfa.seoDescription: RFA mortgage rates from the prime rate page we scrape. RFA Mortgage Corporation does prime loans. RFA Bank of Canada, a Schedule I bank, does alternative loans. Both are broker-only.
rfa.heroIntro: RFA is not a nickname for a person. It is a broker-channel group. The table above is the prime sheet. Alternative pricing from RFA Bank is a separate quote.
rfa.overview:
The initials are easy to expand incorrectly. RFA's own history page says the firm began in 1996 as Realty Financial Advisors, a real-estate investment business, and only later entered residential lending. In 2018 it set out to be a broker-channel lender. In 2019 it bought Street Capital Bank of Canada and, with that charter, became a Schedule I bank as well as a prime mortgage company.

Residential lending is split on purpose. RFA Mortgage Corporation does prime mortgages: insured, insurable, and uninsurable. RFA Bank of Canada is the federally regulated bank and the balance-sheet alternative lender. RFA's about page calls the bank's book Alt-A and B. The Mortgage Corporation page shortens the bank's role to Alt-A. Either way, a bruised-credit or non-prime file is the bank, and a clean insured purchase is the corporation. Brokers are told to know which one they submitted to, because servicing phone numbers differ. Mortgages whose numbers start with 4 are directed to RFA Bank servicing. Numbers starting with 1, 6, 7, 8, or 9 are directed to a different servicing centre for RFA Mortgage Corporation. Guessing from the logo on the rate sheet is how payouts go to the wrong desk.

Distribution is the broker channel. The public prime page is written for brokers: rate holds of 120 days unless a promo says otherwise, no pre-approvals on that sheet, a possible one-time float-down that has to arrive at least ten business days before closing and does not apply to promotional rates, and beacon add-ons (the February 2026 prime sheet added 20 basis points when a primary beacon on an insurable file was under 680). Transfers were marked ineligible under three years, with promo exceptions. Second homes had the same three-year floor. None of those rules are a consumer privilege table. Prepayment percent, double-up, and the penalty formula were not on the pages we used. Ask the broker to pull them from the current commitment package. Do not invent a 20 percent privilege because other monolines have one.

The rate block on this page is scraped from RFA's prime page. You will see insured, insurable, and uninsured rows when RFA published them. Insurable is the in-between category: more than 20 percent down, but still eligible for insurer treatment, often priced nearer the insured special than a true uninsured refinance. Our labels follow the scrape. Alternative RFA Bank pricing is not in that table. If your broker is talking beacon 600 and a lender fee, you are not looking at the five-year insured cell.

desjardins.tagline: A caisse network whose closed mortgages allow 15 percent a year, or a doubled payment, and whose Accord D loans are closed to new borrowers.
desjardins.seoDescription: Desjardins mortgage rates from the live scrape. Closed mortgages allow 15 percent a year or a doubled payment. The Versatile Line splits the financing. New Accord D loans have ended.
desjardins.heroIntro: Desjardins is the cooperative behind the caisses, concentrated in Quebec and present in Ontario. The rows above are our scrape of its mortgage rate page, which mixes a posted shelf and a special.
desjardins.overview:
Desjardins is a cooperative financial group organized around caisses. Members deal with a caisse advisor, in French or in English, rather than with a monoline through a broker. The mortgage footprint that matters for most readers is Quebec, plus Desjardins' Ontario caisse network. If you are buying in another province, ask whether a caisse will take the file before you compare the rate. The group is not a Big Six bank, and it is not a federal credit union in the Coast Capital sense. Deposit protection and the regulator follow the caisse system. Ask the advisor which entity is on the hypothec or mortgage and which deposit scheme applies. We are not going to guess the coverage limit in this paragraph.

A closed mortgage, on Desjardins' own explanation, lets you increase the payment up to double the original payment and prepay up to 15 percent of the initial amount each year, without a prepayment charge. The 15 percent has to be a partial prepayment, minimum $100, and unused room does not carry forward. You can combine the lump sum with a higher payment or with accelerated frequency. An open mortgage can be paid down without that 15 percent ceiling, unless a promotion such as cash back says otherwise. Open rates are usually higher. Prepayment charges show up when you do something the contract did not allow: paying more than the privilege, refinancing early, or breaking a closed term. Desjardins publishes a penalty calculator and tells you the caisse's actual charge can differ from the estimate. We did not find a single public sentence that reduces every caisse's fixed penalty to "three months or IRD, posted versus discounted." Use the calculator, then ask the advisor which comparison rate the caisse uses. The penalty guide is the vocabulary for that question.

The readvanceable-style product still being sold is the Versatile Line of Credit. Desjardins says you can split the financing into several loans, each with its own term, rate, and payment. The rate page prices the line off Desjardins prime plus or minus a spread, then a personalized spread after they look at the file. That is not one blended rate you can paste into our table.

Accord D is the product to stop recommending. Desjardins' page titled as the end of Accord D financing says Accord D loans and Accord D RRSP financing are no longer offered. Existing agreements continue. As of 20 October 2026, installments and prepayments on those older loans route through the credit-card account, and a prepayment can require a phone call because card payments are applied in an order that may not hit the Accord D balance. If a blog still calls Accord D the way to hold a mortgage and a line together, it is describing a closed book.

extraSections.heading: Posted shelf, special, and the caisse's discretion
extraSections.html:
A cooperative can post a rate card that looks like a bank's and still price the member in front of them differently. Desjardins prints both the card and, on some terms, a special. The special is the comparable. The card is what a penalty formula might refer to if the caisse uses a posted comparison rate. That is the question to ask, because we are not going to pretend every caisse uses the same IRD circular. Two members with the same special can face different break fees if their contracts point at different comparison rates.

Bring the written special, the privilege (15 percent and the doubled payment), and the penalty answer to the same meeting. Then look at National Bank's All-in-One if you want a bank's version of a split loan and line. Different institution, different fee, different penalty sentence.

The prepayment page is more specific than "flexible." On most closed mortgages you may prepay up to 20 percent of the original principal once each calendar year. The "You're the Boss Mortgage" raises that to 30 percent of the original principal each loan year, and that 30 percent can be split into more than one payment. You cannot use the privilege inside 30 days of paying the mortgage out. Mortgages whose agreements were prepared before 1 November 2018, and that are not You're the Boss, may be allowed to use the privilege only on the anniversary date. Double-up is separate: on a payment date you can pay up to twice the regular payment, and the extra goes to principal. Closed terms longer than five years are subject only to 90 days' interest as a prepayment penalty after the first five years. That is Coast Capital's wording, and it is a reason to look at a seven- or ten-year term if you might need out in year six.

A variable mortgage keeps the payment flat when Coast Capital's prime moves, until it cannot. More of the payment goes to interest when prime rises. If the payment no longer covers the interest, the trigger rate, Coast Capital can change the payment. That is a different variable design from a lender that reprices the payment at every prime change. Ask which one you are being offered. An open mortgage can be prepaid without a penalty. A closed mortgage that exceeds the privilege, or that is refinanced, renewed early outside the exception, or transferred, can incur one. We did not extract a full IRD formula from the public basics page. The prepayment calculator on the site is an estimate. The agreement is the charge. Phone or book the appointment for the real number.

Renewal has three member-facing promises worth writing down. Inside six months of maturity you can renew early with no penalty. Renewing with Coast Capital does not require you to re-qualify. And you can port the mortgage to a new home, keep the rate and the remaining term, and skip the prepayment penalty if you meet the conditions. Member renewal rates are negotiated with an advisor, not copied from the new-business cells above. A HELOC is offered at up to 65 percent of the home's value, interest only on what you draw, reusable as you repay. It is not a substitute for reading whether the first mortgage is a collateral charge or a conventional charge. Coast Capital publishes a "collateral versus conventional" note with its mortgage documents. Ask which one they will register. A collateral charge is harder to hand to another lender at maturity. The switch guide is the checklist, and it reminds you that a provincial or federal credit union is outside OSFI's straight-switch bulletin. Ask Coast Capital which qualifying rate they would use if you are the one arriving, not leaving.

Early renewal inside six months without penalty
HELOC up to 65 percent of value

coastcapital.whoItsFor:
Coast Capital fits a British Columbia member who wants a credit union, a large annual prepayment, and a renewal path that does not re-underwrite the loan if you stay. You're the Boss is the product to ask for by name if the 30 percent privilege is why you picked them. The port feature matters if you expect to move inside the Lower Mainland or on the Island and would rather keep the rate than pay a penalty and start again.

It is a poor fit outside B.C., or if you need a broker to shop the file nationally and fund with a monoline next week. It is also a poor fit if your property was mortgaged with them before November 2018 and you have been assuming you can prepay on any day. Check the vintage. A high-ratio purchase still follows insurer rules. Use the insurance calculator and the first-time buyer guide for the down-payment side. The credit union does not erase the premium.

products.title: Closed fixed
products.description: Rate and payment fixed for the term. Most files can prepay 20 percent of original principal once a calendar year. You're the Boss can prepay 30 percent per loan year, in one payment or several. Double-up sits alongside. After year five of a longer term, the penalty cap they publish is 90 days' interest.

products.title: Variable
products.description: Tied to Coast Capital prime. The payment is designed to stay the same while the split between principal and interest moves. A trigger rate can force a higher payment if interest is no longer covered. That is the risk to price, not a surprise the credit union invented in the fine print without telling you. Their basics page says it in plain language.

products.title: HELOC
products.description: Up to 65 percent of the home's value. Interest only on the drawn amount. Redraw as you repay. Access through digital banking, the app, ATM, cheque, or a branch. It is a separate facility from the mortgage privilege. Drawing the line is not a mortgage prepayment.

products.title: Renewal and port
products.description: Early renewal with no penalty when you are six months or fewer from maturity. No re-qualification if you stay. Port to another property and keep the rate and term if you qualify. Member rates on renewal can differ from the new-business scrape. Ask for both numbers.

coastcapital.howRatesCompare:
Our Coast Capital scrape is usually a five-year conversation: fixed and variable, insured and uninsured, when those four cells are published. There is often no three-year or one-year row. Absence is the feed, not a statement that an advisor cannot quote another term.

Compare the insured five-year with Vancity and the insured hub, and the uninsured five-year with the uninsured hub and the Vancouver banks. Credit-union pricing in B.C. sometimes leads a bank special and sometimes does not. The 30 percent privilege, the six-month early renewal, and the flat variable payment are the reasons a slightly higher rate can still be the better contract. The Vancouver and Victoria pages are the local context. They do not replace the membership conversation.
shoppingTips: Ask if the offer is a standard mortgage at 20 percent or a You're the Boss mortgage at 30 percent. The name is the privilege.
If the mortgage started before 1 November 2018, ask whether lump sums are allowed only on the anniversary.
On a variable, ask what the trigger rate is today and what happens to the payment if prime rises through it.
Ask collateral or conventional before you sign. Coast Capital has a document on the difference because it changes a later switch.
Inside six months of maturity, get the early-renewal offer and a competitor quote on the same day. The no-penalty window is the cheap time to decide.

extraSections.heading: Federal credit union, B.C. mortgage
extraSections.html:
"Federal" describes the charter, not a national branch map. Coast Capital's mortgage business is a British Columbia membership business. The HELOC, the renewal promises, and the prepayment bands are published for that membership. A borrower moving to Alberta does not take the credit union with them the way a Big Six bank follows a transfer. Porting, on their renewal page, is about bringing the same mortgage to a new home while remaining with Coast Capital, which implies the new home still fits their lending area. Confirm the new city before you rely on the port to avoid a penalty.

Deposit insurance for a federal credit union is not the same sentence as CDIC for a Schedule I bank, and it is not the same sentence as a provincial credit-union scheme. Ask the branch which scheme covers your deposits and whether the mortgage entity is the same legal name. Then decide the rate. The lender-type guide is the background, not a substitute for that answer.

faqs.question: Is Coast Capital a bank?
faqs.answer: No. Coast Capital Savings is a federal credit union, member-owned, lending in British Columbia. You join as a member. It is not Scotiabank or Vancity, and a federal charter does not mean it originates mortgages in every province.

faqs.question: How much can I prepay?
faqs.answer: Most closed mortgages: up to 20 percent of the original principal once each calendar year. You're the Boss: up to 30 percent each loan year, in one or more payments. You also can double a regular payment. Do not use the privilege in the 30 days before a full payout. Agreements prepared before 1 November 2018 may be limited to the anniversary date unless they are You're the Boss.

faqs.question: What happens to a variable payment when prime rises?
faqs.answer: Coast Capital says the payment stays the same and more of it goes to interest, until the payment no longer covers the interest. At that trigger rate the credit union can adjust the payment. Ask for the trigger on your rate before you choose variable over fixed.

faqs.question: Can I renew early without a penalty?
faqs.answer: Yes, on Coast Capital's renewal page, if you are six months or less from maturity. Staying also means you do not re-qualify. The member renewal rate can differ from the new-business rates in the table. A port to a new home can keep the existing rate and term if you qualify.

faqs.question: Does the HELOC go to 80 percent?
faqs.answer: Coast Capital's line-of-credit page says a home equity line up to 65 percent of the home's value, with interest on the amount you use. It does not advertise an 80 percent readvanceable plan. If you need more, ask what combined mortgage-plus-line limit they will actually register, and whether the charge will be collateral.

atb.name: ATB Financial
atb.tagline: Alberta's financial institution, built for Albertans.

atb.overview:
ATB Financial is Alberta's provincially owned financial institution—a Crown corporation of the Government of Alberta, not one of the federally chartered Big Five banks. It takes deposits and makes loans for Albertans, with a branch and advisor network that is meant to cover Calgary, Edmonton, smaller cities, and rural communities, including agricultural borrowers that national banks sometimes treat as a specialty file.

ATB offers closed fixed and variable residential mortgages and home equity lines of credit. Because it is provincially regulated, its uninsured underwriting can differ from OSFI Guideline B-20 even though insured (high-ratio) mortgages still have to satisfy CMHC, Sagen, or Canada Guaranty—including a qualifying-rate test. Alberta buyers also skip provincial land transfer tax; estimate remaining cash to close with the closing costs calculator after you pick a price.

atb.whoItsFor:
ATB is for people whose home and banking life are in Alberta: city purchases in Calgary or Edmonton, smaller centres, and rural or farm properties where local knowledge of land, income, and seasonal cash flow matters. If you do not live in Alberta and are not buying there, ATB is generally the wrong lender to pursue.

Choose ATB when you want an Alberta-based advisor, possibly a HELOC, or an agricultural/rural discussion that a Toronto call centre will not own. Choose a national bank or a brokered monoline when you need a lender that follows you to another province or when a broker can show a clearly lower insured 5-year on the same file. Run the stress test calculator anyway—insurers still apply GDS/TDS on high-ratio deals.

Some weeks a Big Five special in Calgary undercuts ATB; some files (rural, relationship, uninsured conventional) look better in-house. faqs.question: What are current ATB mortgage rates?

faqs.question: Can I get an ATB mortgage if I do not live in Alberta?
faqs.answer: ATB Financial is built for Albertans and Alberta property. If you live in another province and are not buying in Alberta, you should look at national banks, credit unions in your province, or brokered lenders instead. Eligibility for specific programs is ATB's to confirm.

faqs.question: Is ATB a bank?
faqs.answer: ATB is a financial institution wholly owned by the Province of Alberta. It is not a federal Schedule I bank like TD or Manulife Bank. faqs.question: Does ATB use the federal mortgage stress test?

faqs.question: Does Alberta have land transfer tax?

faqs.question: How do ATB mortgage rates compare with the big banks?

faqs.question: Can ATB help with a farm or rural property?

equitable.name: Equitable Bank
equitable.tagline: A Schedule I challenger bank that sells mortgages only through brokers, including alternative, HELOC, and reverse.
equitable.seoDescription: Equitable Bank mortgage rates from the EQ Bank residential page we scrape. Mortgages are broker-only. Alternative files, the HELOC, and reverse mortgages are separate from that table.
equitable.heroIntro: Equitable Bank lends to homeowners through mortgage brokers, under the EQ Bank name. The uninsured fixed rows above are the public residential scrape. They are not the alternative rate sheet.
equitable.overview:
EQ Bank is a trade name of Equitable Bank, a Schedule I bank. The head office on its product sheets is EQ Bank Tower at 2200–25 Ontario Street in Toronto. The consumer mortgage page calls the institution Canada's Challenger Bank and says the mortgages are available solely through professional mortgage brokers. There is no branch where you book a residential mortgage the way you would at a Big Six. EQ Bank's deposit app and the mortgage are related brands and different applications. Do not assume a savings-account login is a mortgage application.

The product list on that page is wider than a prime five-year. Fixed-rate mortgages, adjustable-rate mortgages, a home equity line of credit, and reverse mortgages are all named. So is commercial lending. The "you're more than a credit score" section points at self-employed borrowers, limited credit, newcomers, rental investors, and people earning foreign income. That is alternative and near-prime work, priced by a broker, not by copying the public rate card.

The alternative single-family sheet, marked for brokers and dated in 2026, is the concrete version. Purchases, refinances, ports, equity take-outs, and title transfers. One-to-four unit homes and condos. Maximum loan-to-value 80 percent, amortization up to 30 years, minimum beacon 500 with lower scores considered, standard debt ratios 50/50 and an extended-ratio product at 60/60 in select markets. Qualification is described as the contract rate plus 2 percent. A standard alternative deal carries a 1 percent commitment fee, with no-fee options available. Rate hold 90 days. Gifted down payments and a previous bankruptcy can be considered. Business-for-self files can be documented with bank statements or financials rather than only T4s. Those are program specs for brokers. They move. Your approval is the spec that counts.

The HELOC sheet is just as specific, and it has a hard geographic limit: not available in Quebec. First position up to 65 percent of value or a $1 million limit. Second position only behind an EQ Bank mortgage, combined loan-to-value up to 80 percent, the line itself still capped at 65 percent. It will not sit behind another lender. Owner-occupied or rental. Interest-only, qualified at contract plus 2 percent. The Equitable Bank Visa access card is how draws work. A reverse mortgage is offered for homeowners who want equity out with no monthly payment. It is a different contract from the HELOC, with its own age and loan-to-value rules. Ask the broker for the current reverse term sheet rather than treating a blog summary as the offer.

Beacon 500 considered, lower case by case
HELOC cannot go behind another lender's mortgage
Public rate page is not the alternative grid
equitable.whoItsFor:
Equitable fits a borrower whose broker needs a bank that will read business financials, a rental portfolio, a thin credit file, or a newcomer's foreign income, and who accepts a fee and a shorter hold as part of that. It also fits a homeowner who wants a HELOC or a reverse mortgage from the same group, outside Quebec for the line.

It is the wrong first call if you are a salaried borrower with a straightforward insured purchase and you only want the lowest five-year special. That file belongs in a prime monoline comparison. The uninsured fixed cells on this page might be in the conversation. The alternative sheet is not, unless the prime lenders have already said no. Use the lender-type guide to keep prime, alternative, and reverse from blurring together.

products.title: Residential fixed and adjustable

Self-employed, rentals, gifted down payments, and prior bankruptcies are named as in-scope. Confirm the current sheet.

products.description: Not in Quebec. Up to 65 percent standalone, or behind an EQ Bank mortgage only, to a combined 80 percent. Interest-only. $1 million limit on the sheet we reviewed. A line behind a different bank's mortgage is a no.

equitable.howRatesCompare:
The Equitable rows in our file are uninsured fixed terms from the residential rate page, often one year through five. There is no insured column and no variable column in that scrape. Do not invent them. Compare a five-year uninsured cell with other uninsured conventional rates on the uninsured hub, and remember a prime monoline's insured special is a different product.

An alternative quote should be compared with Home Trust and with CMLS Aveo on fee, term, beacon, and loan-to-value, not on the public card. A 1 percent commitment fee on a standard alternative deal belongs in the refinance calculator beside the rate. Leaving it out makes Equitable look cheaper than the commitment.

On an alternative file, get the commitment fee, the hold (90 days on the sheet we saw), and the qualifying rate (contract plus 2) in the same email as the rate.
If you want a HELOC behind a mortgage you already have elsewhere, Equitable's sheet says no. The line goes behind an EQ Bank mortgage or stands alone.
Quebec files cannot use the EQ Bank HELOC. Ask what, if anything, they will do on the mortgage itself in that province.
Reverse mortgages are a separate product. Do not compare the reverse quote with the five-year fixed cell.

extraSections.heading: Challenger bank still means a broker
extraSections.html:
Equitable's size and its Schedule I charter tempt people to shop it like TD. The distribution is the opposite. The mortgage page says the loans are available solely through brokers. The alternative specs are watermarked for brokers. A salaried borrower who wants a relationship discount for moving a chequing account is in the wrong lineup. A self-employed borrower with twelve months of business statements is in the lineup the sheet describes.

EQ Bank's savings brand is how many people meet the name. The mortgage does not come with the savings rate, and the savings account does not waive the commitment fee. Keep the two offers on two pieces of paper. Then read the stress-test guide for the federal qualifying-rate background, and ask the broker whether your file is being qualified at contract-plus-2, at the insured stress test, or under a stated exception. The sheet and the guide answer different questions.

faqs.question: Is EQ Bank the same as Equitable Bank?
faqs.answer: EQ Bank is a trade name of Equitable Bank. Deposits and the mortgage brand share the name. The mortgage is originated by brokers. A savings account at EQ Bank is not an application for the mortgage and does not set the mortgage rate.

faqs.answer: Equitable says its mortgages are available solely through mortgage brokers. The path is a broker who has the prime or alternative shelf, not a branch appointment.

hometrust.heroIntro: Home Trust lends through mortgage brokers, not a branch. The insured and uninsured rows above are the public rate scrape. Alternative pricing and the Equityline Visa are separate conversations.
hometrust.overview:
Home Trust Company has lent to borrowers who do not fit a bank template for decades. Home Bank, a subsidiary, describes Home Trust as serving Canadians since 1987, and describes itself as a subsidiary of Home Trust. Home Trust's place in the corporate stack changed on 8 January 2025, when Fairstone Bank of Canada and Home Trust closed the combination they had announced in March 2024. The parent is Fairstone Bank. The family of brands named in that release includes Home Trust, Oaken Financial, Home Bank, Fairstone, Eden Park, and Fig. Smith Financial Corporation holds a majority voting interest. Centerbridge, the Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan Board, and management were described as minority shareholders. Oaken is the direct-to-consumer deposit brand. It is not the mortgage application. The mortgage still goes through a broker.

Home Trust's broker page says it works with an exclusive group of mortgage brokers, not with every brokerage in the country. The problems it names are specific: business-for-self and commission income, low or limited credit, high-value urban and suburban property, condominiums, rentals, and newcomers. The same page also describes competitive rates for clients with strong credit who are buying, financing a rental, or switching. So the shelf is both alternative and a prime-style option for cleaner files. We are not going to attach a product nickname to the prime relaunch unless Home Trust's own page is the source. If your broker says a particular prime program is back, ask for the guideline. The public rate table is not that guideline.

The Equityline Visa is the product that does not have a twin at a monoline. Home Trust describes it as a HELOC alternative: access to equity through a Visa, without breaking the first mortgage. It can be combined with a Classic first mortgage under one charge so later equity is available for renovations, a tax bill, or an operating float. There is also a Preferred Visa aimed at everyday spending, including for first-time buyers and self-employed clients, and a Secured Visa for people establishing credit. Those cards are not mortgage rates. They are why a broker might place the first mortgage here even when the rate is not the lowest on the street: the charge can leave room for the card. Ask whether your file is a one-charge Equityline structure or a standalone mortgage. A one-charge collateral-style registration is harder to move to another lender later. The switch guide is the warning.

Prepayment percentages and the penalty formula were not in the public pages we relied on. Home Trust's alternative and prime programs can differ from each other, and a one-year alternative term often carries a fee and a percent-of-balance charge rather than a big-bank IRD. Ask the broker for the clause on the program they actually submitted. Do not copy CMLS Aveo's 3/2/1 schedule or a bank's posted-rate IRD onto Home Trust because both are "alternative."

Home Trust fits a borrower who has already been told a bank will not use their income the way they earn it: commissions, a new corporation, a beacon still recovering, or a newcomer without a Canadian score.
