Compare Home Trust's insured cells with other insured postings on the insured hub, and the uninsured cells with the uninsured hub, but only after the broker says those cells are the program you qualify for. An insured Home Trust five-year can look like a prime monoline. An uninsured cell that is much higher can be an alternative or a posted rate. The table does not label the underwriting guide.

For a declined bank file, the comparison set is Equitable Bank, RFA Bank, and CMLS Aveo. Match beacon, loan-to-value, fee, and term. A lower rate with a 2 percent fee can lose to a slightly higher rate with no fee by the second year. Do the arithmetic. Do not let the brand stack (Fairstone, Smith Financial, Oaken) substitute for it.
shoppingTips: Confirm your broker is actually onboarded with Home Trust. The panel is not open to every licence.
Ask which legal entity will be on title, Home Trust or Home Bank, and whether Fairstone is only the parent.
If Equityline is part of the pitch, ask whether it is one charge with the mortgage. One charge changes the exit.
Get the lender fee, the term, and the prepayment charge for the specific program. We do not publish a Home Trust privilege percent because we did not verify one.
Oaken rates are deposit rates. They are not a discount on the mortgage.

extraSections.heading: Parent company is not the servicer you call
extraSections.html:
After 8 January 2025 the group sits under Fairstone Bank, with Stephen Smith's firm holding majority voting control. Day to day, a mortgage borrower still deals with Home Trust or Home Bank servicing and with the broker who submitted the file. Oaken is where some people hold a GIC. Mixing those phone numbers is how a payout request gets lost during a refinance.

The Equityline Visa is the operational quirk worth planning around. If it shares a charge with the first mortgage, paying the mortgage off does not automatically free the title while the card balance remains. Ask, before you sign, what has to be zero before a discharge. That question belongs in the same meeting as the rate. The penalty guide covers the first-mortgage break. It does not know your card balance.

faqs.question: Is Home Trust a bank?
faqs.answer: Home Trust Company is a trust company. Home Bank is a subsidiary of Home Trust. Since 8 January 2025, Home Trust has been part of Fairstone Bank of Canada. Smith Financial Corporation holds majority voting control of that group. Your mortgage documents will name Home Trust or Home Bank, not a branch of a Big Six bank. Oaken Financial is the deposit brand.

faqs.question: Can any broker get me a Home Trust mortgage?
faqs.answer: No. Home Trust says it works with an exclusive group of brokers. If your broker is not onboarded, they cannot submit the file, regardless of the rate on this page. Ask them.

faqs.question: What is the Equityline Visa?
faqs.answer: Home Trust's Visa secured by your home, so you can draw equity without breaking the first mortgage. It can be registered together with a Classic mortgage on one charge. The card rate is not in the mortgage table. A shared charge can complicate a later switch until both balances are dealt with.

faqs.question: Does Home Trust only do bad-credit mortgages?
faqs.answer: No. The broker page covers both clients with limited credit, self-employment, or newcomer status, and clients with strong credit who are buying, financing a rental, or switching. The rate and the fee follow the program. Ask which program produced the quote.

faqs.question: Why is the uninsured rate so different from the insured rate?
faqs.answer: Because the scrape records two different postings. They may be different programs, different risk, or a special versus a posted rate. We do not collapse them. Ask the broker which cell, if either, applies to your down payment and your beacon.

truenorth.tagline: A brokerage that shops other lenders, with a written beat-or-$500 rule and its own THINK Financial lender in Quebec.
truenorth.seoDescription: True North Mortgage rates from the live scrape. True North is a brokerage. Its beat-or-$500 rule has conditions, and the funding lender sets the penalty. Quebec files can use THINK Financial.
truenorth.heroIntro: True North Mortgage is a brokerage. The insured and uninsured rows above are a scrape of the rates it publishes. The lender on your commitment is the company that can charge you a penalty.
truenorth.overview:
True North Mortgage is a Canadian mortgage brokerage. The people you deal with are licensed to shop lenders. They are not the Big Six, and they are not the name on a standard charge unless the file is funded by a lender they own or arrange. Provincial licensing, on True North's own disclaimer, is Ontario licence 12700, British Columbia and Alberta under True North Mortgage Inc., and Saskatchewan licence 316409. The firm also publishes a Quebec rate page and says it now offers brokerage services in Quebec. If your province is not on the disclaimer and not on a current rate page, ask before you apply. A national advertisement is not a licence.

The rate block we store comes from True North's Ontario rate page. Insured and uninsured fixed terms from six months through five years show up there, plus five-year variables. A six-month posting can be a short-term special that has nothing to do with the five-year rate. Do not let the shortest cell set your expectation for a five-year term. Our meta description uses the five-year figures from the scrape for that reason, and it does not treat them as a promise.

True North's Lowest Rate Guarantee is a written program, not a mood. You apply with them first and qualify under the federal stress test. You then have seven calendar days to bring a firm offer of a lower rate on a similar mortgage: primary residence, same property, same term, same loan amount, same or lower closing costs. Cash-back and "effective rate" offers from a competitor do not count. Second mortgages do not count. The property has to be inside their designated lending area. If they cannot match a qualifying offer and you close with the other lender on those terms, they pay $500. They decide eligibility. The guarantee applies to their fixed-rate applications. Read the current page before you rely on a screenshot of this summary. This website does not pay the $500 and does not match anyone's rate.

In Quebec, True North says clients can be placed with THINK Financial, which it describes as its in-house, CMHC-approved lender, alongside other lenders it shops. A THINK mortgage is a lender contract. Privilege, penalty, and renewal sit with THINK, even if a True North broker arranged it. Elsewhere, the funding lender might be a bank, a monoline, or a credit union. True North says its brokers are salaried rather than commissioned, that volume is used to buy the rate down, and that a hold can run up to 120 days depending on the lender. "Depending on the lender" is the important half of that sentence. A hold is only as long as the funder allows.

truenorth.whoItsFor:
True North fits a borrower who wants a brokerage to post a rate, put a salaried broker on the file, and stand behind a written match-or-$500 rule on a straightforward primary-home fixed mortgage. It fits a Quebec borrower who is willing to have THINK Financial, or another lender they shop, on the paperwork.

It is a poor fit if you need a second mortgage, a cash-back competitor matched dollar for dollar, or a property outside the lending area in the guarantee. It is a poor fit if you will not name the funding lender. The rate is True North's advertisement. The penalty is the lender's. Read the penalty guide after you know which institution you are actually borrowing from. Self-employed and alternative files may be placeable. They are not automatically priced at the insured special in the table.

products.title: Brokered fixed and variable
products.description: Terms True North publishes, funded by a lender they arrange. Our Ontario scrape includes short fixed terms through five years, insured and uninsured, and five-year variables. The lender's privilege and penalty are the product features. Ask for them before you compare a tenth of a point.

products.title: THINK Financial
products.description: True North's in-house lender, described on the Quebec page as CMHC-approved. A THINK commitment is not a generic "True North mortgage." Prepayment, default insurance, and renewal are THINK's. Ask when the file is THINK and when it is a third-party lender.

products.title: Rate hold
products.description: True North says a rate can be held up to 120 days, depending on the lender, for a purchase, renewal, or refinance. The cap is the funder's cap. Get the date in writing. A hold that expires before a long closing is not a hold.

products.title: The guarantee's boundaries
products.description: Fixed-rate applications, first lien, primary home, seven days, similar costs, no competitor cash-back, no second mortgage, inside the designated area. $500 only if you close with the other lender after True North cannot match. Their discretion. Not a promise from this website.

truenorth.howRatesCompare:
Use the True North block as a brokerage's advertised grid, split by insured and uninsured. Compare a five-year insured cell with nesto, Butler (also labelled insured here), and the insured hub. Compare the uninsured five-year with the uninsured hub and with a bank special on the same label. The six-month rate is a different product. Leave it out of a five-year argument.

True North's pages say their rates run lower, on average, than banks and other competitors. That is their claim. The cell above is the checkable part. A brokerage average does not survive contact with your beacon, your province, or a collateral charge. Once the lender is named, compare that lender's penalty with the posted-rate guide if the funder is a bank, or with the monoline's own IRD if the funder is First National or a peer.
shoppingTips: Get the funding lender's name. If it is THINK Financial, read THINK's privilege, not a generic broker brochure.
If you intend to use the guarantee, apply there first, keep the competitor's firm offer inside seven days, and make sure the competitor's offer is not cash-back.
Match insured with insured. A 20-percent-down refinance is the uninsured column.
Ask how long the hold is for the lender they picked, not the maximum they mention.
Renewals: take the bank's letter to them if you want a broker bid, and read the renewal playbook so you know which moves re-trigger qualification.

extraSections.heading: A posted brokerage rate is still someone else's contract
extraSections.html:
True North can advertise a five-year number because a lender gave it that number, for a defined borrower, in a defined province. The mortgage you sign uses that lender's charge, that lender's prepayment percent, and that lender's break fee. Salaried brokers change the sales incentive. They do not change the standard charge into a collateral charge or the reverse. Ask the question anyway.

The guarantee is narrow on purpose. It throws out competitor cash-back, second liens, and offers that are not on a primary home with the same costs. Borrowers who shop a cash-back bank special against a True North rate and expect a match are outside the program they think they are in. Bring a clean rate comparison, same term, same insurance status, or do not bother with the seven-day clock. The negotiation guide is about the conversation with a bank. It is not the guarantee.

faqs.question: Is True North Mortgage a lender?
faqs.answer: True North is a mortgage brokerage. It shops lenders and, in Quebec, points clients at THINK Financial as an in-house CMHC-approved lender. The company named on your mortgage is the one that can charge a penalty and the one you will renew with. Ask which it is.

faqs.question: How does the rate guarantee work?
faqs.answer: Apply with True North first and qualify. Within seven calendar days, bring a firm offer of a lower rate on a similar first mortgage: primary home, same property, term, and amount, with the same or lower costs. Cash-back offers and second mortgages do not qualify. If True North cannot match and you close with the other lender, the program pays $500. True North decides eligibility. This site does not.

faqs.question: Which provinces are covered?
faqs.answer: True North's disclaimer lists Ontario licence 12700, British Columbia and Alberta under True North Mortgage Inc., and Saskatchewan licence 316409. It also publishes Quebec rates and says brokerage services are available there. Confirm your property's province on the current site. A licence in one province does not move with you.

faqs.question: What is THINK Financial?
faqs.answer: True North describes THINK Financial as its in-house, CMHC-approved lender, offered alongside other lenders it shops, including on Quebec files. If THINK is the funder, THINK's terms govern prepayment and renewal. Get that commitment, not a screenshot of True North's rate page.

faqs.question: Why is the six-month rate so different from the five-year?
faqs.answer: They are different terms. A short fixed special can be much lower than a five-year commitment and can reset long before you wanted to renegotiate. Compare five-year with five-year. The table shows both so you can see the gap. It is not one blended offer.

faqs.question: Are the rates in the table a promise of the lowest rate in Canada?
faqs.answer: No. They are the figures we scraped from True North's published Ontario rates, split into insured and uninsured. True North's own guarantee is a separate, conditional program. Qualification, province, property, and the funding lender all move the rate you can actually have.
